items.title: French policing under scrutiny as student protest injuries mount
items.author: Juliette Jabkhiro, Layli Foroudi
items.creator: Juliette Jabkhiro, Layli Foroudi
items.summary: Fourteen-year-old Eden suffered a broken jaw and multiple smashed teeth when he was struck by a tear gas canister directed towards him at close range by a police officer last week during student protests in France, his parents and family lawyer said.
items.body:
Fourteen-year-old Eden suffered a broken jaw and multiple smashed teeth when he was struck by a tear gas canister directed towards him at close range by a police officer last week during student protests in France, his parents and family lawyer said.
The teenager had been sitting on a wall looking at his phone metres away from the protest in Saint-Ouen-l'Aumone, the lawyer said. An officer approached him and struck him with a baton, prompting Eden to respond with a kick, according to the local prosecutor. A second officer then fired a tear gas grenade with a Cougar launcher, hitting him in the face.
"(The officer) shot him in the mouth and left him lying on the ground, without even calling the emergency services," said lawyer Elsa Marcel. The family, who asked for Eden's second name to be withheld to protect their privacy, has filed a complaint for attempted murder, she said.
A police spokesperson said they do not comment on ongoing investigations. According to the prosecutor’s office, the police officer said that he was seeking to protect himself and his colleagues after the student confronted police. The officer was placed under formal investigation on charges of assault by a public official resulting in permanent disability or disfigurement on Tuesday, eight days after the incident.
The case is one of 24 under investigation by the IGPN internal police watchdog linked to the policing of a more-than-two-week-long wave of [USN:L8N45S08G TEXT:"student unrest"] over [USN:L6N45M1EJ TEXT:"conditions"] in schools. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu has described the demonstrations as the most violent in decades.
The police response has renewed calls for the withdrawal of the use of rubber bullets and grenade launchers, which are not used by police in many other European countries and have been repeatedly criticised in recent years by rights groups, including Amnesty International and UN human rights experts, as dangerous and disproportionate.
It has also sparked anger among the public and fanned support for a protest movement that is the latest manifestation of deep-seated [USN:L8N45L0FB TEXT:"discontent"] with President Emmanuel Macron’s government ahead of a 2027 election.
Via interviews and reviews of legal documents, Reuters has documented 28 cases of injuries suffered due to police force, of which 15 are among those under investigation by the IGPN. They involve the use of rubber bullets, stun grenades, tear gas, batons and charges on horseback.
In two cases, a person's eye has been lost or injured due to rubber bullets. In another, a 15-year-old in Lens had his hand blown off — likely by a stun grenade, according to interior minister Laurent Nunez, who [USN:L1N45T0B2 TEXT:"paused"] the use of stun grenades pending an investigation into the case.
Nunez said on Wednesday in a radio interview that about 200 students had been injured, but that it was very rarely the result of police action. “Our primary role is, of course, to protect high school students,” he said.
Authorities said that 700 police officers have also been injured, schools have been burned or ransacked, and teachers and members of the public have been attacked. The police have arrested 6,877 people, mostly minors.
“France is an anomaly in terms of its use of arms and the number of victims — we have four irreversible injuries in the space of 12 days, and they are minors,” said Sebastian Roche, researcher on policing at the French National Centre for Scientific Research.
“It is a level that is unknown in (France’s) contemporary history,” he said.
CALLS TO BAN 'LESS LETHAL' WEAPONS Roche said that France stands out in Europe for its use of "less lethal" weapons such as rubber bullets and stun grenades. Such weapons are generally not used for public order policing in Britain, Italy and Germany, aside from Hamburg, and although permitted in Spain, have caused fewer injuries than in France, said Roche.
In the Paris suburb of Argenteuil, a 16-year-old student on his way home after finding his school closed was shot by police, injuring his left eye, which may be permanently damaged, his lawyer Sophia Kerbaa told Reuters. It is not clear if he was hit by a rubber bullet or something else, she added.
A video viewed by Reuters showed the boy bleeding from his eye.
“He was in the wrong place at the wrong time ... he is injured and in shock,” Kerbaa said.
The prosecutor investigating the case said that, according to the police account, the injured student “seemed to correspond” to one of two young people who had directed fireworks at police officers, who responded with rubber bullets.
The interior ministry did not respond to questions on the case, or that of Eden.
Human rights advocates, including Amnesty International, and some politicians have called for “less lethal” weapons to be banned permanently, while police unions say the police need these weapons to enforce order in violent situations and to ensure their own security.
“We must withdraw the use of rubber bullets and ... aim for zero injured students. That will allow us to de-escalate,” Mayor Bally Bagayoko of the left-wing France Unbowed party [USN:L6N45T13Z TEXT:"told Reuters"]. Bagayoko joined the protests in his town Saint-Denis, saying he wanted to protect young people from the police.
Thierry Clair, a police union representative, said that serious injuries such as Eden’s, or another child losing his hand, were tragedies, but should not call into question France’s policing techniques. He said the problem came instead from the intensity of the violence being committed by some young people who stoked tensions.
“How do we respond when people are moving towards confrontation? If we remove intermediate force options, all we are left with is lethal force,” Clair told Reuters. “That is simply inconceivable.”

items.title: Germany's firewall against the far-right AfD feels the heat
items.author: James Mackenzie, Andreas Rinke
items.creator: James Mackenzie, Andreas Rinke
items.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz's warning this week that extremism was entering Germany's parliamentary system was the latest in a series of signs that mainstream parties' "firewall" to isolate the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) has begun to buckle.
items.body:
Chancellor Friedrich Merz's [USN:L8N45T15N TEXT:"warning"] this week that extremism was entering Germany's parliamentary system was the latest in a series of signs that mainstream parties' "firewall" to isolate the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) has begun to buckle.
This week, at least four lawmakers from mainstream parties in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt appear to have defied party orders and voted to give the AfD, which wants to restrict immigration and restore energy ties with Russia, its first regional assembly speaker.
The ballot was secret but suspicion immediately fell on the 15 members of Merz's conservative Christian Democrats (CDU) in parliament, who had been told to abstain.
Karin Prien, deputy chair of the national CDU, said if CDU lawmakers were to blame, "there must be consequences".
The AfD itself, which has been leading the CDU in nationwide surveys for more than a year and declared its aim of winning a national election due in 2029, hailed a "political turning point".
"For the first time, it was clear that the so-called 'firewall' doesn't have to be stronger than the freedom of action of members of parliament," said Martin Reichardt, head of the AfD in Saxony-Anhalt.
COULD AFD WIN A NATIONAL ELECTION IN GERMANY? The AfD's [USN:L1N44Y01V TEXT:"record victory"] last month has alarmed rivals, who consider it an anti-democratic party opposed to the values that helped Germany to rebuild after World War Two and renounce the horrors of Nazism and its nationalist, racist ideology. The AfD rejects their label of "extreme right" as a slur.
Across Europe and beyond, the result, which left the AfD just short of an absolute majority in the state parliament, was seen as one of the clearest indications yet that it could win a national election in 2029.
Merz's coalition with the centre-left Social Democrats in Berlin has been under increasing strain, riven by disagreements and sliding in opinion polls as voters, like many across Western Europe, blame the mainstream parties for declining living standards.
On Wednesday, the parties held talks to iron out differences over issues including pensions and tax, and said they were "determined not to hand our country over to extremists".
Set up over a decade ago during the euro zone debt crisis, the AfD has grown from a fringe movement into the most popular party in Germany in opinion polls.
Yet parts of the AfD - including its Saxony-Anhalt branch - have been designated as extremist by German security services, meaning that they are considered to be opposed to constitutional principles of human rights, democracy and the rule of law.
The Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution (BfV), the domestic intelligence agency, compiled a 1,100-page confidential report last year that found the AfD incited resentment of migrants, as well as racism and Islamophobia.
For its part, the AfD says it is restoring German national pride and values, and ensuring that migrants are not prioritised at the expense of German citizens.
So far, the "firewall" approach - under which the established parties have refused to cooperate with the AfD - has kept it from joining any coalition government.
In Saxony-Anhalt, where it needs three more seats for a majority, it is still [USN:L8N45S000 TEXT:"unclear"] how it can form a government after talks over a possible coalition with the populist far-left BSW made no progress.
FEARS OF COOPERATION WITH AFD However, the AfD's Ulrich Siegmund, who dismisses the firewall as "childish", says he can persuade enough members of other parties to defy party orders to enable him to be confirmed as [USN:L8N4500A1 TEXT:"state premier"] by the end of the year.
In this week's speaker ballot, the AfD's Tobias Rausch won 48 votes - four more than the combined total held by the AfD and the BSW.
Merz has ruled out any arrangement with the AfD, which he says aims to destroy the CDU, and the issue is expected to be discussed at a CDU's leadership meeting on Sunday and Monday.
But whether it remains realistic to refuse to cooperate with a party attracting almost a third of the vote, and more in the formerly communist eastern states where it is strongest, has become an urgent question.
CDU deputy leader Prien said any sign of accommodation could open divisions that could "jeopardise the very existence of the entire party".
The AfD has gained ground nationwide but remains weaker in western Germany than in the east, and appears unlikely to repeat its Saxony-Anhalt result in state elections next year.
However, the problems that have helped create the conditions for its rapid rise resist easy answers. War in Ukraine has cut off the supply of cheap energy that fuelled Germany's economy while competition from China has eaten away at its once-invincible industrial base.
Economists warn continually that fundamental reforms are needed to pensions and taxes to meet the needs of an ageing population, while deep divisions remain between the eastern and western regions, almost four decades after the fall of the Berlin Wall.
Marking the anniversary last week of German reunification in 1990, President Frank-Walter Steinmeier acknowledged that many felt overlooked by the political system and that a generalised feeling of insecurity had undermined confidence.
But, in an unusually bleak assessment, he said the bitter political climate was threatening to send Germany back into the chaos that ended the democracy of the prewar Weimar Republic.
"Today is about the survival of democracy," he said. "We must stand up for what remains important."

items.title: New Zealand's O'Rourke ruled out of India series
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: New Zealand fast-bowler Will O'Rourke will miss the series against India as he continues his rehabilitation from injuries to his left hamstring and calf, the country's cricket board said on Saturday.
items.body:
New Zealand fast-bowler Will O'Rourke will miss the series against India as he continues his rehabilitation from injuries to his left hamstring and calf, the country's cricket board said on Saturday.
O'Rourke suffered a hamstring tear during New Zealand's test series win over England in June, before hurting his calf in training in late August.
The 25-year-old will aim to return to full fitness ahead of a four-test tour of neighbours Australia beginning on December 9.
"It's obviously disappointing for Will to have to miss such a marquee tour at home against India," New Zealand coach Rob Walter said in a statement.
"He was set to feature in both the ODI and test series, but following subsequent discussions, we all agreed it was best for him to take some more time to rehabilitate both injuries and safely build up his bowling loads.
"Our pace bowling resources will be critical over the next few months so we're taking a conservative approach to Will's return to ensure he's fully fit before he takes the field again."
New Zealand host India in five Twenty20 internationals, five one-day internationals and two tests, with the opening T20 in Christchurch on October 22.

items.title: Kyle Busch's 11-year-old son does burnouts at Charlotte memorial event
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Brexton Busch honored his late father, Kyle Busch, in an appropriate manner during a celebration of life on Friday, doing burnouts at Charlotte Motor Speedway.
items.body:
Brexton Busch honored his late father, Kyle Busch, in an appropriate manner during a celebration of life on Friday, doing burnouts at Charlotte Motor Speedway.
The youngster was behind the wheel of the No. 8 Richard Childress Racing Chevrolet when he drove in front of 10,000-plus fans and performed burnouts until the rear tires went flat.
Brexton Busch then climbed onto the roof of the car and acknowledged the crowd. His 4-year-old sister, Lennix, handed him a checkered flag, which Brexton then waved atop the car while taking a bow -- his father's signature victory celebration.
Kyle Busch died unexpectedly on May 21 at age 41 of complications from severe bacterial pneumonia and sepsis.
During the Friday event, Kyle Busch's brother Kurt, also a NASCAR champion, team owner Joe Gibbs and drivers including Austin Dillon and Kyle Larson discussed Kyle Busch's legacy.
Samantha Busch, Kyle's widow, was the last to speak.
"I keep thinking how lucky I was to know every single version of him, the young racer who took me around Indianapolis Motor Speedway when I was just 21 years old, and little did we know, it'd be the ride of our lifetime," Samantha Busch said. "The fierce competitor who basically thought second was last, and threw our kids ridiculously high in the air, a tradition that they loved and I feared every single time. The team owner who gave others a chance, Rowdy who loved his fans more than anything, and of course, stirring up things, and the dad who found so much joy and pride in his children. ...
"This is not the end of Kyle's story. His story continues every time we give a young racer a chance, share something he taught us, or tell the next generation what made Rowdy unforgettable. Years from now, I hope people remember Kyle as one of NASCAR's greatest drivers. He worked his entire life for that. But I also hope they meet someone whose life is better because Kyle was here."
Kyle Busch won the NASCAR Cup Series championship in 2015 and 2019. His total of 234 victories in NASCAR's top three series, including 63 in the Cup Series, is an all-time record.
RCR has paused use of the No. 8 Chevrolet after Kyle Busch's death, saying the number is reserved for use by Brexton Busch "when he is ready to go NASCAR racing."
--Field Level Media

items.title: Indian police detain 'cockroach' movement founder Abhijeet Dipke
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were also detained.
items.body:
Police in the Indian capital Delhi detained the founder of the Cockroach Janta Party, Abhijeet Dipke, on Saturday, ahead of a protest called by the youth movement demanding the resignation of the country’s chief election commissioner, the party said.
TV channels reported earlier that police officers met Dipke at the Delhi airport after he arrived from the financial capital Mumbai and asked him to call off the protest as authorities had banned it.
CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were also detained from their flight upon landing, the movement said in a statement.

items.title: RBI opens special dollar window for oil firms as rupee comes under pressure
items.author: Manojit Saha
items.summary: Special window for PSU oil companies from Monday; Forex dealers will not permit users to rebook any foreign exchange derivatives ...
items.body: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Saturday announced a host of measures to support the rupee, which is trading close to its all-time low, including a special window to meet the dollar demand of three state-run oil marketing companies (OMCs). The three OMCs are Indian Oil Corporation Ltd (IOC), Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd (HPCL) and Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL). “On the basis of assessment of current market conditions, Reserve Bank of India has decided to open a special window to meet the entire daily dollar requirements of three public sector oil marketing companies,” the RBI said in a press release on Saturday. Under the facility, the RBI will sell dollars to the public sector OMCs through designated banks. The facility will come into effect from October 12, 2026, and will remain in place until further notice, the central bank said. The central bank has also announced regulatory measures for the foreign exchange market and imposed restrictions on the rebooking of cancelled foreign exchange derivative contracts. “Authorised Dealers shall not permit users to rebook any foreign exchange derivative contract involving INR, whether deliverable or non-deliverable, which has been cancelled with any Authorised Dealer after the issuance of the Directions,” the RBI said. Rollover of foreign exchange derivative contracts on maturity will continue to be permitted. The RBI has also reduced the threshold for undertaking foreign exchange derivative transactions without establishing an underlying exposure to $5 million from $100 million. “The corresponding threshold for taking positions in exchange-traded currency derivatives involving INR, without establishing the existence of underlying exposure, has also been reduced from $100 million to $5 million equivalent, across all Recognised Stock Exchanges taken together,” it said. The central bank also introduced a Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve (FERR), requiring forex dealers to maintain a reserve equal to 20 per cent of the notional amount of each eligible derivative transaction involving the rupee. “This FERR shall be applicable for foreign exchange derivative contracts involving INR undertaken to hedge current account exposures where the user purchases foreign currency against the INR,” the RBI said. The central bank said the measures were intended to strengthen market discipline and ensure appropriate risk management in the foreign exchange market, while maintaining an orderly and transparent market environment. The Indian currency has come under pressure since the West Asia conflict began in late February, depreciating 6 per cent. Over the past year, the rupee has depreciated by more than 8 per cent. The central bank has been heavily intervening in the foreign exchange market to curb volatility. India’s foreign exchange reserves declined by about $51.1 billion in the four weeks ended October 2 after touching a record $785.7 billion in the week ended September 4.

items.title: 中国、1─9月の都市部新規雇用1052万人　サービス業支援へ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [北京 １０日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[北京 １０日 ロイター] - 中国人力資源・社会保障省は１０日、１─９月の都市部の新規雇用者数が１０５２万人となり、年間目標の８７．７％を達成したと発表した。同省は、サービス業の雇用拡大に向けた新たな措置を計画している。

同省当局者は記者会見で、１─８月の都市部の調査失業率は平均５．２％で、雇用は「おおむね安定」していたと説明した。

李忠次官兼報道官は、他部門と連携しサービス業の発展を通じて雇用を促進する政策文書を策定する方針を示し、サービス業が雇用吸収の主要な受け皿としての機能を一段と発揮できるようにすると述べた。

李氏はまた、労働集約型産業で雇用を安定的に維持するとともに、新興産業や将来有望な産業で新たな雇用機会を模索していくと表明した。

items.title: Jocelyn Bioh on why Broadway is finally ready for 'School Girls'
items.author: Kathryn Lurie
items.creator: Kathryn Lurie
items.summary: The playwright and actor talks beauty, colorism, and how Broadway has changed in the decade since she wrote the play.
items.body:
Playwright Jocelyn Bioh during an interview with Reuters in New York City. REUTERS/Brendan McDermid Nearly a decade after Jocelyn Bioh wrote “School Girls; Or, The African Mean Girls Play,” the play itself has barely changed. But the world around it has.
The comedy about a group of teenage girls at a Ghanaian boarding school premiered off-Broadway in 2017, launching Bioh’s career as a playwright and going on to become a hit at regional theaters across the United States. But despite its success, Bioh was told it might not belong on Broadway.
Now “School Girls” has made it there — following the Broadway success of Bioh’s “Jaja’s African Hair Braiding” in 2023 — and she is finding an audience that responds differently to the play’s exploration of body image, the privileging of lighter skin, known as colorism, and the often brutal social dynamics of girlhood. Beneath its rapid-fire jokes and teenage rivalries is a more painful story about who gets to be considered beautiful — and what people are willing to do to fit that ideal.
Speaking in New York City, Bioh discusses what has changed since “School Girls” was first produced, the universality of teenage insecurity and why bringing the play to Broadway feels like coming full circle.
This conversation has been edited and condensed for clarity.

How does it feel to finally bring “School Girls” to Broadway?
It feels incredibly humbling. This play changed my life. It was the first play of mine that ever got produced. I can very clearly mark what my life was like before opening night of that show and then after.
That audiences and critics all still feel the same way nearly a decade later is a reminder that I was on the right track.
It also feels doubly exciting because even though it had so much success regionally and has been all over the country, I was told, “It's a great play, but maybe it's not the right fit for a Broadway stage.”

What do you think was meant by that, and what has changed enough for it to be on Broadway now?
Broadway shows were very specific then. They didn't have ensembles that looked like the cast of “School Girls.” It was a lot of celebrities, a lot of things that seemed to fit into one specific category or box.
The world has shifted. Audiences are different than they were 10 years ago. In a lot of ways, “Jaja's African Hair Braiding” having so much success was a marker that, a Broadway play is just a play that's on Broadway. It doesn't necessarily have to fit a specific category.

Is there anything in the play that hits differently than it did when you first wrote it?
The conversation around beauty standards and body image has shifted in the last 10 years. Some would say (for the) better, some would say worse, but we're all aware of it in a different way.
The play kicks off with Paulina bullying Nana about her size and her eating. You can feel the audience is immediately on Nana's side. Halfway through the play, she has a moment where she really stands up to Paulina, and every night that moment gets applause. You can feel the audience cheering, almost jumping up ready to fight with her. They're taking off their earrings!
We did not have that experience off-Broadway. I think we were in a time where we accepted the idea that if you were somebody who was bigger, you should be losing weight; you should be trying to conform. Our ideas of beauty are very different now. Big ships turn slow, but I appreciate that I can feel that in the audience.
Did you rewrite much for this production?
Very small things, little jokes that I thought would land better. But the play is still largely the same thing I wrote in 2016.
If I were sitting down to write this play now, I don't know that I would be as honest or as vulnerable as I was then, particularly in the moments where Paulina is speaking very directly about how colorism has affected her life. I think I would censor myself a little bit now. I never thought the play would get produced, so I was very free and vulnerable in a way.

Playwright Jocelyn Bioh. REUTERS/Brendan McDermid Why?
When you're a playwright and your name starts to grow within the community, you start to have an awareness of the responsibility of your words. And I'm okay with having that responsibility because I know I'm doing something really different. I'm really blowing open how people see Black and African people on a theatrical stage. There's an incredible responsibility to that.
The play takes place in Ghana, but these girls feel instantly recognizable. Did you know when you were writing it how universal they would be?
I understood that there's a real rich universality we have, particularly in school and friendship dynamics. Those things are evergreen and universal.
I knew what I was writing was different, (that) the girls and the people I was reflecting were different, but I didn't want to alienate audiences. That's part of why I added the subtitle. What's something we all know and recognize about the teenage experience? Mean girls.
Paulina seems to believe that if she can just become Miss Ghana, she can escape the limits of her life. Is her obsession with beauty really an obsession with power and possibility?
Probably. Ultimately, I think she really believes this is going to set her up for a successful life in entertainment.
The play is set in 1986, and if you became Miss Ghana, Miss World, Miss Universe — any of those things — you could become a star. This is how we have Vanessa Williams or Halle Berry or Kenya Moore, if you're of the “Real Housewives” persuasion.
(Another character,) Eloise, is a former Miss Ghana and did leave. She's come back now living a different life, (signifying that) in order to have success, you've got to get out. In order to have power, you have to get out. Maybe Paulina doesn't see the beauty and power that she can build in her own country.
That's reflective of so many immigrant, particularly African immigrant, stories: In order to have success, you need to leave. I don't know if the play were set in 2026, (if) that would be the case now. I think the play would be very different. But for Paulina and her circumstances then, that is what she believed.
The play deals so directly with colorism. Do you think colorism is in some ways more sensitive to talk about than racism?
They're inextricably linked. The play largely talks about and shows the effects of colorism, but then ends with a global lesson on racism.
And we've not moved on from it. When we started rehearsals for the play in August, the biggest news story was Lupita Nyong'o playing Helen of Troy in Christopher Nolan's film (“The Odyssey”). (Her casting) did not fit with whomever's standard of beauty (for) the woman whose face launched a thousand ships. Why didn't it fit? Why were there so many suggestions about, “Well, Zendaya's in the movie, why can't she play that part?” That's a very clear conversation about colorism, whether people are using that word or not.

When I wrote this play, it was really important for me to have that conversation because it had affected my life so much. Revisiting it now, especially in relation to these conversations that are happening globally, I'm like, well, we've not moved on from it. We can't move on from colorism because nobody's moved on from racism.
I can't change people's minds. But if people come to see “School Girls” and their implicit bias can shift just a little bit, then I've done my job.
The play is extremely funny until you realize how much pain is sitting underneath the humor. How deliberate is that?
I really believe that comedy is just a funny way of being serious. Humor and pain are on two different sides of a truth coin. It's all rooted in truth.
Paulina is a girl in the world who's trying to be affirmed and validated that she belongs there, that her beauty is widely accepted even if she knows that it's not. The lengths she goes to get there are what's comical, but it's rooted in something real that we all experience.
At the end of the day, I'm a comedic writer and I want people to be entertained. But because I know the responsibility of who I'm introducing and the culture I'm introducing, I think there's a responsibility in also educating people. If I can make that medicine go down with a little bit of sugar, honey, agave, whatever you like, I'm willing to go there.
The perspectives expressed in Culture Current are the subject’s own and do not necessarily reflect the views of Reuters News.

items.body:
Yimou Lee　Ben Blanchard

[台北 １０日 ロイター] - 台湾の頼清徳総統は１０日、双十節（建国記念日）の演説で、台湾は平和を大切にするが自由を放棄することはないと述べ、台湾の人々が生存する権利は尊重されなければならないと訴えた。防衛力の強化は挑発ではないとも強調した。

台湾は中国から軍事的・政治的圧力の強化に直面している。中国は一貫して台湾を自国領土と主張しているが、台湾は強く反対している。

台湾は防衛費を増額し軍の近代化を進めているが、 対峙する中国軍の規模ははるかに大きく、ステルス戦闘機や空母、多数のミサイルなどの先進的兵器の配備を進めている。 

頼氏は総統府前で演説し、平和は「願い」だけでは実現できないと強調。 

「台湾は平和を大切にするが、自由を放棄しない。交流には前向きだが、従属は受け入れない」と語った。

また、「権威主義の拡張」に直面する中で、台湾の決意は自らの存続だけに関わるものではないと指摘。

「力がルールに優越することはなく、強者が人々から自らの未来を決める権利を奪うことはできないと、国際社会が今も信じているかどうかの問題だ」と続けた。

防衛投資の拡大については、戦争を挑発するためではなく抑止するためだとして、「対話を放棄するためではなく、対等と尊厳を基礎として対話が行われるようにするために自衛力を強化している」と語った。

頼氏が総統として初めて双十節演説を行った２０２４年の直後、中国は台湾周辺で軍事演習を実施したが、昨年は行わなかった。

台湾周辺で中国が最後に軍事演習を行ったのは昨年１２月下旬で、台湾向けとして過去最大となる１１０億ドル規模の米国の武器売却の報道を受けたものだった。

頼氏は、米国と中国が対話を通じて競争を管理し、紛争や戦争のリスクを低減していることを歓迎すると述べた。

items.title: Wall Street Week Ahead: Bank earnings, CPI headline busy markets week as S&P 500 hovers near records
items.author: Reuters
items.summary: U.S. stock investors are on high alert as they anticipate quarterly earnings reports from major banks, including JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs. These reports are pivotal, shedding light on corporate profitability and the future direction of interest rates. The upcoming Consumer Price Index report will also provide vital clues about inflation trends, potentially swaying Federal Reserve policy.
items.body: Quarterly earnings reports from banks, along with inflation data and other economic releases next week, will offer US stock investors insight into the strength of corporate profits and the path of interest rates, two factors influencing the market's rally.On Tuesday, the S&P 500 hit an all-time closing high, its first since mid-August. Its year-to-date gain has swelled to more than 14%.Wednesday's Consumer Price Index report, perhaps the most closely watched inflation gauge, is among the last key data releases before the Federal Reserve meets at the end of October to decide whether to raise interest rates. The Fed hiked rates last month for the first time since 2023 to try to contain inflation.Banks including JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs will report next week, kicking off what is expected to be an exceptionally strong quarter overall for US corporate profits. Following a robust first half, S&P 500 earnings are expected to have jumped by more than 30% in the third quarter, according to LSEG IBES. Earnings have been incredible this year, and we're just going to have to start to see with the banks how Q3 shaped up, said Matthew Miskin, co-chief investment strategist at Manulife John Hancock Investments.Banks To Give Views On Consumer, Capital MarketsJPMorgan, Goldman, Citigroup and Wells Fargo will report results on Tuesday. Morgan Stanley and Bank of America are set to report the following day, rounding out reports from the six largest banks.Banks typically kick off quarterly earnings season, and the reports offer important views into the health of the overall US economy.Matt Stucky, chief portfolio manager of equities at Northwestern Mutual Wealth Management, said he would focus on how higher interest rates are rippling through to capital markets and consumer spending. We've seen rates back up. We've seen energy costs back up, Stucky said. And the question is, how is this impacting the consumer? Heading into the reports, bank stocks have been among the worst-performing groups recently amid a rise in Treasury yields, with the S&P 500 banks index down 7.5% in the past month. Is the market sniffing out something that is underneath the surface for these financial companies? Miskin said. I think there's going to be a sigh of relief if these financial services companies come out with good results next week. Other earnings reports next week include healthcare companies Johnson & Johnson and UnitedHealth Group , and asset manager BlackRock.Could Cpi Revive Rate-Hike Bets?Wednesday's September CPI report is expected to show a 3.7% rise on an annual basis, according to a Reuters poll. The core measure, excluding volatile energy and food components, is estimated to increase by a more modest 2.5%. The Fed targets a 2% annual inflation rate.Michael Reynolds, vice president of investment strategy at Glenmede, said he was concerned with sticky services inflation that has been showing up in reports. We really want to see material progress on (core services inflation) to get a little bit more confident that the Fed doesn't have to be as aggressive as maybe the market's pricing in, Reynolds said.Reports next week on producer prices and retail sales will give a fuller picture of the economy. Traders have reduced expectations the Fed will increase rates again at its October 27-28 meeting. But data that shows a hotter economy could revive hiking bets, investors said. If you start to see more evidence of re-accelerating inflation that's not going to come down absent a full hiking cycle from the Fed, that's where equity markets really can be under pressure, Stucky said.The Fed's move to start hiking rates has been one factor pushing Treasury yields higher. The benchmark 10-year yield was around 5.24% late on Friday, after recently reaching its highest level in 24 years.Higher yields pose a number of obstacles for equity performance, including by making bonds more competitive investments and by pressuring stock valuations. While a 5% yield on the 10-year Treasury had been seen as a key threshold to create stock pressure, the market has avoided any significant downside thus far as yields have breached that level and then moved even higher. At some point, major indices are going to cry uncle on higher rates, Reynolds said.

items.title: Trackhouse's Fernandez takes first pole at Indonesian GP
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Trackhouse rider Raul Fernandez grabbed a career-first pole at the Indonesian Grand Prix on Saturday, with title contenders Jorge Martin and Marc Marquez set to start on the second row.
items.body:
Trackhouse rider Raul Fernandez grabbed a career-first pole at the Indonesian Grand Prix on Saturday, with title contenders Jorge Martin and Marc Marquez set to start on the second row.
Fernandez, who won the British MotoGP in August, finished quickest with a lap of one minute 28.852 seconds -- 0.109 quicker than Aprilia's Marco Bezzecchi.
"Too many times, I was very close to taking pole (in the past)," said Fernandez, who also set a lap record during practice on Friday.
"Yesterday, I started to feel super comfortable with the bike. This morning, to be honest, I didn't really feel like that.
"I just tried to be calm, tried to not be nervous. Now we have a very good opportunity, let's try to enjoy and let's try to fight for the victory."
VR46 Racing's Fabio Di Giannantonio completed the front row with a strong display on his birthday.
Bezzecchi was content with second place despite having to abandon what looked set to be a pole-winning lap when yellow flags were waved following a Fermin Aldeguer crash.
"I'm very happy. It was a good job this morning in practice, but also in the qualifying, I was confident on the bike," the Italian said.
"Unfortunately, I met a yellow flag in the second stint, but I'm very, very happy, satisfied. It's a very good first row for this afternoon, but also for tomorrow."
Defending champion Marquez of Ducati was fourth-quickest, just ahead of title rival and championship leader Martin of Aprilia.
With six rounds remaining in the season, including the Indonesian MotoGP, the outcome of the championship is hanging on a knife-edge as Martin sits on 333 points - just two above Marquez.
Marquez will fancy his chances of closing that gap this weekend, but the weight of history is against him, with the Spaniard having a disastrous record at the Mandalika circuit, where he has never completed a full MotoGP race.
Last year, he suffered a season-ending collarbone injury in the race after a crunching collision with Bezzecchi on the opening lap.

items.title: Euro falls, set for fifth straight weekly drop as oil prices rise
items.author: Reuters
items.summary: The euro has experienced a significant drop as concerns about France's public debt continue to affect investor confidence. Global bond markets have stabilized following US President Donald Trump's remarks on potential military action against Iran. Oil prices fluctuated significantly, impacting market dynamics and investor sentiment. US consumer sentiment has worsened amid rising living costs attributed to the ongoing Middle East conflict.
items.body: The euro was poised for a fifth straight weekly drop on Friday, with early gains fading as oil prices erased earlier declines, but recent selling pressure was muted as France's beleaguered bond market steadied.The euro zone's currency hit a 17-month low of $1.1161 on Monday as investors worried about France's record public debt and the difficult political path to budget cuts, in contrast with a robust-looking US economy and currency.The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, rose 0.13% to 102.25. The index was up about 0.3% on the week and on track for a fourth straight weekly gain, its longest run since May 2025.The euro was last down 0.1% at $1.1198, and off about 0.5% on the week as it was poised for its longest streak of weekly declines against the dollar since the start of 2025.Risk premiums on French and Italian government debt were on track for a weekly decline after jumping in late September, as investors looked for fresh developments before demanding higher compensation for fiscal and political risks.Trump Signals No Iran AttackGlobal bond markets had calmed earlier on Friday as oil prices fell after US President Donald Trump said that the US would not attack Iran before US midterm elections on November 3 and added that there had been productive talks with Tehran over the war. As it stands right now, you have a confluence of factors - you have higher oil prices, you have the issue in France, so it is really tough to say what is moving the market more than the other, said Eugene Epstein, head of trading and structured products at Moneycorp in Stamford, Connecticut. But practically speaking, I'd say today is in a relative holding pattern, everyone is just waiting for all the Fed speak to make its way through, because certainly you can see that the sensitivity of the dollar is high to the entire range of Fed speakers now, Epstein said.Crude prices moved off their lows, however, as British navy-affiliated agency UKMTO said a vessel was struck by an unknown projectile 13 nautical miles west of Al Jazeera in the United Arab Emirates.US crude rose 0.6% to $92.04 a barrel after falling as low as $90.01 and Brent advanced to $104.88 per barrel, up 0.58% on the day, after declining to $102.33.Bond yields around the world have climbed in recent weeks due to expectations of central bank rate hikes as well as concerns about government finances.Central Bank Policy In FocusBut expectations for a rate hike from the Fed at its policy meeting later this month remain subdued, with markets pricing in a 19.4% chance for a rate hike of at least 25 basis points, according to CME FedWatch, even as recent economic data has pointed to persistent inflation pressure. However, investors are pricing in an 85.8% chance for a hike at the central bank's December meeting.On Friday, the University of Michigan's Surveys of Consumers showed US consumer sentiment slumped further in early October as the rising cost of living because of the Middle East conflict soured households' views of the economy.While many Fed officials have indicated more rate hikes will be needed to curb inflation, others have pushed back on the need for immediate hikes, and suggested the Fed should be patient and flexible in deciding the rate path.French debt has been under pressure as politicians struggle to curb the budget deficit ahead of a divisive election in 2027. The calling of a snap election in Spain earlier in the week also added to the pressure on the euro.Sterling gained 0.08% to $1.3235 but was on track for a seventh straight week of declines, its longest stretch since November 2024.Against the yen, the dollar strengthened 0.25% to 158.25. The Japanese currency was on pace for its fourth straight weekly decline against the greenback, down about 0.2% on the week.

items.title: Modi at 25: Small signs, big challenge
items.author: Shekhar Gupta
items.summary: Multiple headwinds make the turbulence Mr Modi is battling as he steps into his 26th year in public office. This has brought the three-point Modi proposition under the greatest pressure since 2014 ...
items.body: This is the season of looking at Narendra Modi’s 25 years in power and beyond. His followers are celebrating. His Cabinet has passed a resolution praising him. Of course, the critics are out dissecting his quarter-century in public life, not with a scalpel but with a scythe. It’s also the season for people, especially journalists, telling their “when I first met Modi” stories. I’ll hold on to mine for another day. Let’s not risk diluting today’s serious argument. Two weeks ago, we noted that for any incumbent in India, the third year of a term is the toughest. This is when challenges build up, fatigue sets in, aspiring successors sharpen the knives. We also said that the last of these doesn’t apply to Mr Modi. Nobody in his party would even dare to whisper the “S” word. The third year of Mr Modi’s third term, however, is beset with all of the other challenges. His tired and incomplete Cabinet is struggling. His chief ministers — barring Yogi Adityanath, Devendra Fadnavis and Himanta Biswa Sarma — aren’t up to the multiple challenges. Having used the ancient editorial privilege of ‘tabooing’ a word, and listing the cliched “narrative” under it, I then can’t use it. The fact is, this market of popular opinion is rife with competing, contradictory notions. The Modi-BJP story is still the most significant. It just isn’t as dominant as before. Multiple breezes make the turbulence Mr Modi is battling as he steps into his 26th year in public office. This has brought the classical — and so far all-conquering — three-point Modi proposition under the greatest pressure since 2014. The three points are: Hard, Hinduised nationalism; ever-expanding welfare, distributed efficiently, with minimal friction or leakage; and visible construction of physical infrastructure. All of this without significant overhang of corruption. The Modi proposition survives. It’s just that several other factors have now emerged. And we aren’t just talking about the rebellion of an irreverential, ageist, educated and mostly not-impoverished GenZ.  What makes this period of crisis unprecedented in Mr Modi’s prime ministership is the convergence of these factors.. Like the Shakespearean “when sorrows come, they come not single spies, but in battalions.” In isolation, each of these factors may look small. But they become formidable when the big picture comes together. As the great management guru late C K Prahalad used to say: “Weak signals add up to a big change.” He elaborated this in his oft-quoted 1995 paper “Weak Signals Versus Strong Paradigms” (Sage Journals). Prahalad himself summarised it thus: “Taken one at a time, these signals don’t add up to much. But taken together, they present a picture of a country (or industry) in dramatic transformation.” Is this what Mr Modi is confronted with now? Let’s check out some facts. I am reducing these “battalions of sorrows” to a dozen most significant. 1. Dramatic damage to the credibility of the Election Commission of India (ECI), and thereby growing doubts over the integrity of the election process. 2. A growing belief that the top judiciary either doesn’t dare look the executive in the eye, or gives wishy-washy orders. Worse, that it speaks with a forked tongue. Ironically, this view is shared on both sides. 3. A solitary retired civil servant (Subhash Chandra Garg) has triggered a nationwide debate on the credibility of gross domestic product figures. 4. Inflation, as now forecast by the RBI, is set to rise to its highest level in nearly three years, and the rupee is struggling despite a highly successful, if expensive, dollar-deposit scheme. 5. Two of this establishment’s most trusted civil servants, the two Election Commissioners (ECs), protected their own backs by creating a paper trail to record their opposition to the Chief Election Commissioner’s decisions. 6. Ability of the Opposition, especially Rahul Gandhi, to lay siege to the Capital with English TV channels and Hindi newspapers, including the ones ‘most trusted’ by the establishment, giving it prominent airtime. 7. Young people lampooning the Prime Minister with mere feckless pushback from his “Right-wing” supporters, and an overnight phenomenon like CJP setting the agenda, from Neet to the state of government schools. 8. A small ally like Chirag Paswan taking a swipe at Bihar government over law and order. And a way smaller ally, Om Prakash Rajbhar, going public with his purported conversation with the Prime Minister on Uttar Pradesh’s division into multiple states, which Yogi Adityanath firmly opposes. 9. Contrary to the Modi government’s decisive image, we’ve seen festering indecisiveness —whether to press ahead with delimitation, or what to do with a Parliament session that has not been prorogued even two months after its adjournment sine die. To the naked eye, it shows a lack of confidence in marshalling the numbers for constitutional amendments the BJP really wants.  10. Inability, one can also add prolonged hesitation in carrying out a Cabinet reshuffle, or at least filling the vacant slots. There are too many of them, including education. 11. Continued value destruction in the stock market across Mr Modi’s third term, even as all global peers, from the US and Europe to Japan, South Korea, China and even Pakistan, have boomed. The disinclination to acknowledge the challenge is a self-destructive cop-out when millions from the middle class have moved their savings into systematic investment plans and are celebrated by the government for doing so. It also amounts to them having given the fleeing foreign portfolio investors (FPI), a golden handshake. 12. And finally, a global situation for India not seen in decades. Donald Trump has narrowed India’s strategic space in many areas. He’s also challenging our claims to strategic autonomy, with a provocation a day. Beyond Mr Trump, the war in Ukraine, smouldering West Asia, roiled energy markets, and a newly opened strategic-rentier window for Pakistan. All of these have come on top of a deficient monsoon. That’s beyond any government’s control. But these simmering discontents will play out in a below-average farming year. The larger issues, however, are rooted in the three most fundamental factors that have made India cohesive, and stronger over the decades. These are trust in the Constitution and the belief that nobody can take it away, fairness of the top judiciary, and independence of the Election Commission. All three are under strain now. The BJP knows better than its opponents how badly it was damaged in 2024 by rumours fed by just the odd statement from its middling functionaries and the Ayodhya candidate that the party needed 400 seats to change the Constitution. Now most Indians have not read the Constitution, or even the 106 amendments already carried out. But they see the Constitution almost like a deity or a scripture. Fair, secular, a bill of rights they won’t let anybody take away. Constant talk of special Parliament sessions have brought back these suspicions. The Supreme Court has unfortunately built a well-deserved reputation of flip-flops, cynical prevarications, and talking more than writing. This also applies to its treatment of the SIR issue so far. It’s being watched closely now as it battles multiple challenges—from restoring the credibility of the ECI to taking a view on the right to protest in the Capital. And finally, the ECI. Through nearly eight decades, the institution has had good days and bad, and some indifferent ones. It was, however, never as broken as it is now. An ECI caught in an every-man-for-himself trap will struggle to win back popular confidence. It’s a national crisis. These are the challenges Mr Modi needs to address as he steps into his 26th unbroken year in public office. If he doesn’t, or fails to do so, C.K. Prahalad’s small signals could lead to a dramatic crisis over a very painful two and a half years until the summer of 2029.  By special arrangement with ThePrint

items.title: Panama hit by strongest quake in 75 years, 7.7-magnitude tremor strikes
items.author: Bloomberg
items.summary: The earthquake struck Herrera Province more than 193 km southwest of the Panama Canal, with a 6.6-magnitude aftershock and eight others of magnitude 4.8 or higher recorded ...
items.body: By Carolina Pulice and Lauren Rosenthal Panama was hit by its strongest earthquake in more than seven decades on Friday, followed by powerful aftershocks, as President José Raúl Mulino said no deaths had been reported immediately after the quake. The 7.7-magnitude quake struck Herrera Province, more than 120 miles (193 kilometers) southwest of the Panama Canal, according to the US Geological Survey. Economic losses in the region are likely to exceed $1 billion, according to an early USGS estimate. The earthquake was the strongest to hit that part of Panama since at least 1951, according to the US National Earthquake Information Center. It struck at a depth of 12.6 kilometers, the USGS said. A magnitude-6.6 aftershock hit west of the initial quake late Friday afternoon, according to preliminary USGS readings. Another eight aftershocks have been recorded at magnitude 4.8 strength or higher. The first earthquake was caused by a rupture along a major plate boundary on the Ring of Fire, the seismically active zone that encircles the Pacific Ocean. The mechanism resembled a strike-slip event, in which tectonic plates grind past each other horizontally, according to Jonathan Tytell, a geophysicist at the US National Earthquake Information Center. “It was a very messy event, and shallow, which is not good,” Tytell said. “The energy is right there at the surface and it doesn’t really have time or distance to dissipate.” The USGS initially registered an 8.0 magnitude before revising it. Panama’s geological institute reported the quake as a 7.2-magnitude.  Immediately following the quake, the Pacific Tsunami Warning Center said waves of one to three meters (3.3 to 9.8 feet) above tide level were possible along parts of Panama’s coast. As of 2:42 p.m. local time, all warnings had been lifted. The Panama Canal said operations were continuing normally, with emergency protocols activated and technical teams inspecting facilities for possible damage. The quake was felt as far away as several Colombian cities, including Medellín, according to local media. In Panama, people evacuated buildings, businesses, schools and homes across several regions, local newspaper La Prensa said. Panama’s Tocumen International Airport was closed follwoing the quake but was later reopened. Mulino said the government was mobilising personnel, resources and aid for people affected by the quake, and ordered ministries and public agencies to respond immediately and take preventive measures. Emergency officials were expected to hold a news conference to provide an update on the impact.  When touring the affected area Friday, Mulino told reporters that efforts were being made to relocate families away from impacted dwellings. Analysis was also being done about moving patients out of damaged hospitals.Panama’s Finance Minister Felipe Chapman said he contacted the World Bank, the International Monetary Fund and other banks “to obtain the necessary resources to face this crisis.” Corporación Andina de Fomento, known as CAF, one of the contacted institutions, said it was donating $250,000 to Panama for earthquake relief. Mulino thanked CAF for the “promt help.” People stood barefoot or shirtless in the streets as aftershocks continued, said Cibeles De Freitas, a communications representative for the local unit of First Quantum Minerals Ltd. “There’s a lot of fear because we’re not used to earthquakes in Panama,” she said. “We’re OK, just very scared.” First Quantum Minerals said on social media that the infrastructure at Cobre Panama, its partially idled copper mine, located about 140 kilometers north of the epicenter, remained stable and safe following earthquake.  Panama City’s Metro said lines 1 and 2 were temporarily shut down because of the earthquake. Panama’s firefighters said there were no reports of deaths or injuries in the immediate aftermath of the quake. AES Panama, a unit of AES Corp., the country’s top electricity supplier, said through a spokesperson that its hydroelectric, gas-fired and renewable power plants were operational. Activities at the Trans-Panama oil pipeline were continuing normally after the quake, according to a statement from its operator. Friday’s quake was the latest to hit Latin America in recent months. Venezuela was struck by twin earthquakes in late June that killed nearly 6,500 people and caused widespread destruction along its northern coast. In Colombia, an Aug. 10 quake killed more than 330 and prompted an economic emergency as damage was estimated at roughly $10 billion. Venezuela’s acting President Delcy Rodríguez offered assistance to Panama, as did Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella. “Panama is not alone,” De la Espriella said in a post on X, adding that Colombia was ready to provide whatever assistance was needed. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in a social media post he was monitoring the situation, adding that “the State Department is rapidly mobilising resources and personnel to assist.”

items.title: Anthropic's Claude AI carried out unintended actions on US govt websites
items.author: Bloomberg
items.summary: Anthropic disclosed 4 types of unintended AI behaviour, including exploiting software flaws, submitting unauthorised forms and bypassing access restrictions ...
items.body: By Shirin Ghaffary Anthropic PBC said its Claude AI model carried out additional unintended actions on the digital systems of outside organisations, including some US government agencies’ websites, prompting a warning from the Trump administration for artificial intelligence companies to secure their systems. In a report outlining previously undisclosed incidents, Anthropic listed four types of unintended behaviors that the AI has demonstrated, including exploiting basic flaws in software to run commands, submitting forms it should not have and bypassing restrictions to access certain public data. The company said that some of the cases involved websites run by government agencies at the federal, state and local levels, without specifying the agencies. The report did not name the outside entities involved, which Anthropic said was at the request of some of the affected parties.  Anthropic and its rival, OpenAI, have disclosed a spate of incidents in recent months involving their AI models acting in unintended ways, ranging from behaviours like those described in Friday’s report, to hacks of third-party websites. These disclosures have fueled concerns about the security risks of cutting-edge AI. Anthropic said in the report that it sees the behavior as less severe than some other previous incidents involving its AI. “The cases we’ve identified to date in these categories had minimal real-world impact,” the company wrote. In one example of the improper behavior it found, Anthropic said Friday that its Claude Haiku 4.5 model submitted a tip to a local police department about a homicide, stating in the form, “I may have information regarding this case,” and “I recall seeing someone matching the description in the area,” without filling in the site’s name and contact fields. The Philadelphia Police Department disclosed the incident this morning in a press release, the company said. Anthropic also said it briefed the White House on these cases and notified each agency involved. On Friday, Trump administration officials said they were now requiring that AI companies notify affected parties and address security incidents involving their models. “Earlier today, Anthropic contacted the SI Force to disclose the details of various prior incidents that it discovered in late September involving the unauthorised and fraudulent use of government and other systems,” the White House said in a statement from the Super Intelligence Force, a new government unit tasked by President Donald Trump with overseeing AI development and safety.  “The company informed us that these events occurred in the past, the activity has ceased, and there is no ongoing similar activity,” the statement said. Axios reported on the government requirement earlier.  As a result of these uncovered incidents, Anthropic said Friday that it has restricted some types of internet access for its AI models during the testing phase of its training process.

items.summary: Washington quarterback Demond Williams Jr. missed the start of the second half against No. 20 Iowa on Friday due to an apparent left shoulder injury.
items.body:
Washington quarterback Demond Williams Jr. missed the start of the second half against No. 20 Iowa on Friday due to an apparent left shoulder injury.
Williams got hurt while being tackled late in the first half and was undergoing X-rays as the third quarter began, coach Jedd Fisch told sideline reporters.
Elijah Brown, who replaced Williams late in the second quarter, led the Huskies to a touchdown on the opening drive of the second half, cutting the Hawkeyes' lead to 27-10.
Williams completed 6 of 11 passes for 69 yards before exiting. The junior owns a 66.7% completion rate and 1,396 passing yards with eight touchdowns and three interceptions through six games this season.
In his three seasons at Washington, Williams has a 70.1% completion rate, 5,405 passing yards, 41 TD passes and 12 interceptions in 32 games.

items.title: Defenseman Mathew Dumba, 13-year NHL vet, retires at age 32
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Veteran defenseman Mathew Dumba announced his retirement on Friday after 13 NHL seasons.
items.body:
Veteran defenseman Mathew Dumba announced his retirement on Friday after 13 NHL seasons.
A first-round selection (seventh overall) of Minnesota in the 2012 NHL Draft, Dumba played 10 seasons for the Wild.
The winner of the 2019-20 King Clancy Memorial Trophy, which is given annually for leadership qualities on and off the ice and humanitarian work in the community, played 11 games for the Pittsburgh Penguins in 2025-26 before his contract was terminated in April.
"Matt Dumba is officially hanging up his skates after 748 NHL career games," the NHL Players Association posted on social media Friday. "Wishing the former blue liner and 2019-20 King Clancy Memorial Trophy winner the best of luck in his retirement!"
The 32-year-old Regina, Saskatchewan, native tallied 261 points (85 goals, 176 assists) with the Wild (2013-14 to 2022-23), Arizona Coyotes (2023-24), Tampa Bay Lightning (2023-24), Dallas Stars (2024-25) and Pittsburgh. He produced five goals and 10 assists in 54 career playoff games, 49 of which came with Minnesota.
He notched career highs in goals (14), assists (36) and points (50) during the 2017-18 season.
--Field Level Media

items.title: India central bank takes steps to support rupee, opens dollar window for oil companies
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: India's central bank has announced more measures to support the rupee on Saturday after the currency fell to within striking distance of its record low.
items.body:
India's central bank has announced more measures to support the rupee on Saturday after the currency fell to within striking distance of its record low.
The Reserve Bank of India will open a special window to meet the daily dollar requirements of three government oil-marketing companies to ease the pressure on the spot market
Under such an arrangement, used in times of strain on the currency, the RBI provides oil companies dollars directly from its foreign exchange reserves
Indian Oil (IOC.NS) , Hindustan Petroleum (HPCL.NS) and Bharat Petroleum (BPCL.NS) will be allowed to access to access dollars under the facility from Monday, the RBI said
Forex dealers will not permit users to rebook any foreign exchange derivatives, the bank said
The RBI slashed the limit for positions in exchange-traded currency derivatives involving the rupee to $5 million from $100 million
The central bank asked forex dealers to maintain a "foreign exchange risk reserve" for all derivative contracts involving the rupee equal to 20% of the notional amount of each transaction
The RBI has raised dollars and hiked its policy rate, but pressure on the currency has persisted. On Friday, the rupee closed at 96.73 per dollar, barely changed from its previous close, and near its all-time weakest level of 96.96, hit in May
The rupee rallied in the non-deliverable forward market on Saturday, with the one-month dollar/rupee contract falling about 40 paise in very thin trading, one trader said
Addressing oil companies' dollar requirements removes one of the largest sources of demand from the FX market, which should help reduce volatility but it will show up in a depletion of reserves, said Dhiraj Nim, FX strategist at ANZ Bank in Mumbai

items.title: Taiwan cherishes peace but will not give up freedom, president says
items.author: Yimou Lee, Ben Blanchard
items.creator: Yimou Lee, Ben Blanchard
items.summary: Taiwan cherishes peace but will not give up its freedom, and there must be respect for the right of Taiwan's people to exist, President Lai Ching-te said on Saturday in a National Day speech, adding that boosting defences is not a provocation.
items.body:
Taiwan cherishes peace but will not give up its freedom, and there must be respect for the right of Taiwan's people to exist, President Lai Ching-te said on Saturday in a National Day speech, adding that boosting defences is not a provocation.
Democratically governed Taiwan has faced increased military and political pressure from China, which views the island as its own territory over the strong objections of the government in Taipei.
Facing China's far larger military, which is adding advanced new weapons such as stealth-fighter jets, aircraft carriers and a huge array of missiles, Taiwan is ramping up [USN:L4N44V0I5 TEXT:"defence spending"] and modernising its armed forces.
Peace cannot rely solely on "wishes", Lai said outside the Presidential Office. "Taiwan cherishes peace, but we will not give up our freedom. We are open to exchanges, but will not accept subordination."
Taiwan's resolve is not only a matter of its survival in the face of "authoritarian expansion", he added. "It is about whether the international community still believes that force cannot override rules, and that the powerful cannot strip a people of their right to determine their own future."
DEFENCE INVESTMENT NOT 'PROVOCATION' China's Taiwan Affairs Office did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Lai's speech. China, which has never renounced the use of force to bring Taiwan under its control, calls the president a "separatist" and has rebuffed his offers of talks.
The US welcomes Lai's commitment to maintaining peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait, a senior US administration official said, adding, in reference to China, that "a routine speech is no justification for aggressive or coercive actions".
The United States is Taiwan's most important international backer despite the lack of formal diplomatic ties.
Lai said his government's increased investment in defence aimed to deter war, not provoke it.
"And we are strengthening our self-defence not to abandon dialogue, but to ensure that dialogue can take place on the basis of parity and dignity," he told the crowd, where he also watched military displays and dancing performances.
"There must be respect for the right of the people of Taiwan to exist."
US YET TO APPROVE NEW ARMS PACKAGE In 2024, shortly after Lai's first National Day speech as president, China held war games around the island but did not do so last year.
Its last [USN:L1N3Y000J TEXT:"war games"] near Taiwan were in late December, following news of an $11-billion US arms deal for Taipei, the largest ever. US President Donald Trump has yet to approve a second package, worth [USN:L1N45T00J TEXT:"$14 billion."]
Lai said he welcomed the United States and China managing their competition through [USN:L6N45K195 TEXT:"dialogue"] and reducing the risk of conflict and war. But he urged democracies in the Indo-Pacific region to join forces to retain the status quo of peace and stability in the region.
Taiwan's National Day is held on the anniversary of a 1911 uprising that led to the overthrow of China's last imperial dynasty and the establishment of the Republic of China.
The Republican government fled to Taiwan in 1949 after losing a civil war with Mao Zedong's communists, and the Republic of China remains the island's formal name.

items.title: Ducks bounce back, snap Jets' winning streak
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Judd Caulfield, Tim Washe and Mikael Granlund each had a goal and an assist for the visiting Anaheim Ducks in a 5-1 win against the Winnipeg Jets on Friday night.
items.body:
Judd Caulfield, Tim Washe and Mikael Granlund each had a goal and an assist for the visiting Anaheim Ducks in a 5-1 win against the Winnipeg Jets on Friday night.
Sam Colangelo and Nikita Nesterenko also scored, Jeff Malott and Beckett Sennecke contributed two assists apiece, and Lukas Dostal made 15 saves for the Ducks, who were coming off a 5-2 loss to the visiting Edmonton Oilers on Wednesday after winning their first two games of the season.
Kyle Connor scored, and Clay Stevenson made 12 saves in his seventh NHL start for the Jets, who had won three in a row following a season-opening overtime loss to the Boston Bruins.
The Ducks kept their streak alive of scoring first in every game this season when Caulfield gave them a 1-0 lead at 14:41 of the first period.
Malott drove to the net and Stevenson saved his backhand from in close, but Caulfield slid the rebound between his pads for his first NHL goal in his fourth game.
The fourth line struck again in the second period when Washe finished off a feed from Malott on a 2-on-1 to make it 2-0 at 5:20.
The assist gave Malott his first multipoint game in the NHL.
Anaheim stretched the lead to 3-0 at 4:25 of the third. Sennecke drove toward the left post and then backhanded a short feed to Colangelo in front of the crease and he tapped the puck in the net.
Sennecke has three goals and three assists through the first four games of his second season in the NHL.
Anaheim missed out on its first shutout since its season opener on Oct. 12, 2024, a 2-0 win against the San Jose Sharks, when Connor got behind the defense and scored from in close to cut it to 3-1 at 10:36 of the third.
Granlund got the goal back at 14:06 when he hit the net with a slap shot from above the left circle to make it 4-1.
Nesterenko scored into an empty net with 41 seconds left to make it 5-1.
--Field Level Media

中国は６月以降、沿岸警備隊による定期的な巡視を含め、台湾東岸沖での活動を強化している。

台湾の当局者は、中国が軍、準軍事組織、民間の船舶などを重層的に運用し、海上封鎖の可能性を想定した訓練を行っているとみている。

台湾は、封鎖や有事の際に友好国からの補給ルートとして東岸沖の海域を極めて重要と位置付けている。

items.body:
China added 10.52 million urban jobs in the first nine months of the year, meeting 87.7% of its annual target, the labour ministry said on Saturday.
The ministry is also planning new measures to boost hiring in the services sector.
The surveyed urban unemployment rate averaged 5.2% from January to August, and employment remained "generally stable," officials from the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security told a State Council Information Office press conference.
The ministry will work with other departments on a policy document to promote employment through services sector development, enabling services to better act as the main channel for absorbing jobs, Vice Minister and spokesperson Li Zhong said.
Beijing will also work to keep employment steady in labour-intensive industries and look for new job opportunities in emerging and future industries, he added.
As of end-September, 1.079 billion people were enrolled in basic pension insurance. Unemployment insurance covered 251 million people and work-injury insurance covered 327 million.
The three social insurance funds had a combined balance of 11.2 trillion yuan ($1.67 trillion).
($1 = 6.6920 Chinese yuan renminbi)

items.author: CNA
items.summary: "By asserting authorities around maritime areas that Taiwan has peacefully administered for over 70 years, China only exacerbates tensions and undermines the peaceful resolution of issues that it claims to seek," a US State Department spokesperson said.
items.body:

East Asia

US says China's maritime actions off Taiwan 'deeply destabilising'

"By asserting authorities around maritime areas that Taiwan has peacefully administered for over 70 years, China only exacerbates tensions and undermines the peaceful resolution of issues that it claims to seek," a US State Department spokesperson said.

A member of Taiwan military watches as two US-made Chinook helicopters carry giant Taiwanese flags during a rehearsal ahead of Taiwan's National Day celebrations in Taipei, Taiwan, Oct 6, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Ann Wang)

FAST

TAIPEI: China's maritime actions off Taiwan's east coast are "deeply destabilising" and only worsen tension, the US State Department said, after Reuters reported the first known sighting of a Chinese militia boat in those waters in August.
China, which views Taiwan as its own territory, has stepped up activity off the island's east coast since June with regular coast guard patrols.
Officials in Taiwan, which rejects Beijing's sovereignty claims, say they believe China is practicing for a possible maritime blockade using overlapping military, paramilitary and civilian assets.
Taipei regards the area off its east coast as critical to wartime supply routes from allies in the event of a blockade or conflict.

The United States remains concerned by China's activity east of Taiwan, a State Department spokesperson said, responding to a question on the sighting of the militia boat.
"China's actions are deeply destabilising," the spokesperson added.
"By asserting authorities around maritime areas that Taiwan has peacefully administered for over 70 years, China only exacerbates tensions and undermines the peaceful resolution of issues that it claims to seek."
The US urges Beijing to cease its pressure against Taiwan and instead engage in "meaningful dialogue with Taiwan's democratically elected authorities", the spokesperson added.
China's foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment. China recognises no claims of sovereignty by Taiwan, including over waters surrounding it.
The US is Taiwan's most important international backer, though President Donald Trump has yet to approve a new US$14 billion arms sale package for the island.
Taiwan's Coast Guard said in a statement about the militia boat and its accompanying vessels that their activities were all located outside of "restricted waters".
In a practice dating to the 1950s, China's maritime militia, more commonly seen around South China Sea flashpoints, consists of fishing vessels whose crews receive training and support to operate in disputed waters, often alongside coast guard ships.
In June, Britain, France, Germany and the US, all expressed concern over Chinese activities off Taiwan's east coast as a threat to regional stability and freedom of navigation.

items.title: Palmer is committed to England, says Chelsea boss Alonso
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Alonso was asked about Thomas Tuchel's comments that the 24-year-old Palmer "misses too many opportunities" to play in an England shirt.
items.body:
Cole Palmer remains committed to playing for England, Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso insisted after the attacker drew criticism for missing the international break due to injury.
Palmer, left out of England's World Cup squad this year after a persistent groin injury affected his form, was [USN:L6N45A0LA TEXT:"called up by Thomas Tuchel"] for Nations League fixtures against Spain, the Czech Republic and Croatia.
However, Palmer was forced to [USN:L1N45D0F0 TEXT:"pull out of the squad"] due to a recurrence of the issue, with Tuchel saying the 24-year-old "[USN:L6N45H0UO TEXT:"misses too many opportunities"]" to play in an England shirt.
Asked about Tuchel's comments on Friday, Alonso told reporters: "The most important thing for Cole is to be fully fit, that he enjoys his game, that he is feeling OK.
"Whenever he is not, like in the Brentford game, we could see that he was struggling. He's committed but he needs to be fully fit to play. We need him – the club and the national team," the Spaniard added.
He was speaking ahead of a Premier League meeting with Bournemouth.
"Now he's fine. He's been feeling better this week. We use the first two weeks for him to recover. It's a little bit from the pubalgia (groin injury) he had."
Chelsea, 10th in the Premier League standings, host 17th-placed Bournemouth later on Saturday.

items.title: トランプ氏、平和賞逃し批判　「ノルウェーに消えない汚点」
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Jacob Bogage

[シラキュース（米ニューヨーク州） ９日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Jacob Bogage

[シラキュース（米ニューヨーク州） ９日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は９日、ノーベル平和賞を受賞できなかったことへの不満を改めて表明し、恥ずべき不名誉な決定でノーベル委員会の本拠地であるノルウェーに汚点を残したと批判した。

委員会は、２０２６年の平和賞を国際刑事裁判所（ＩＣＣ）の元判事ナビ・ピレイ氏に授与すると発表した。同氏は、イスラエルがパレスチナ自治区ガザでジェノサイド（集団虐殺）を行ったと結論付けた国連報告書の取りまとめを主導した。

トランプ氏はニューヨーク州シラキュースでの選挙集会で、ピレイ氏を「正体不明の人物」と呼び「その人物のことは聞いたこともない。誰も知らなかった」と述べた。

トランプ氏は大統領就任以来毎年、平和賞を受賞できなかったことに失望を表明してきた。

トランプ氏は「これはノルウェーという国と、こうした不名誉で恥ずべき決定を下した人々にとって、消すことのできない汚点だ」と述べた。

その上で、自ら解決に関与したと主張する複数の紛争を列挙。根拠は示さなかったが、韓国と北朝鮮、日本と北朝鮮、中国と台湾の間での戦争勃発の回避に貢献したと主張した。

「ノーベル平和賞の信用は、反民主主義的で、まさに文明の敵である一握りの過激な思想の持ち主によって永遠に失われた。ノルウェーよ、われわれは忘れない」と述べた。

items.title: L'ouragan Isaias s'affaiblit après avoir touché terre en Floride
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: L'ouragan Isaias s'est rapidement affaibli vendredi après avoir touché terre près de Destin, en Floride, a fait savoir vendredi le Centre américain des ouragans (NHC).
items.body:
L'ouragan Isaias s'est rapidement affaibli vendredi après avoir touché terre près de Destin, en Floride, a fait savoir vendredi le Centre américain des ouragans (NHC).
L'ouragan a été rétrogradé en catégorie 1, mais le NHC a mis en garde contre le risque d'ondes de tempête, d'inondations et de crues soudaines.
L'ouragan, soutenu par des vents atteignant 150 kilomètres par heure (km/h), se trouve à environ 165 km à l'ouest-nord-ouest de Panama City, en Floride, a précisé le NHC.
Isaias devrait traverser l'Alabama et la vallée du Tennessee durant le week-end, a ajouté l'agence.
En Floride, près de 380.000 personnes étaient privées d'électricité, tandis que dans l'Alabama, plus de 210.000 foyers n'avaient plus de courant, montrait le site internet Poweroutage.us.
"Des déclarations d'urgence ont été approuvées en Floride et dans l'Alabama afin de garantir des ressources fédérales après le passage d'Isaias", a dit le secrétaire américain à la Sécurité intérieure, Markwayne Mullin.
Les services d'urgence de Floride avaient appelé la population à rester à l'abri lorsqu'Isaias a touché terre, alors qu'il était classé comme un ouragan de catégorie 2.
