items.title: Cam Talbot, Kent Johnson power Jackets' shootout win over Penguins
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Kent Johnson scored in the first round of the shootout and Cam Talbot made it stand up in his season debut, fueling the host Columbus Blue Jackets to a 3-2 victory over the Pittsburgh Penguins on Friday.
items.body:
Kent Johnson scored in the first round of the shootout and Cam Talbot made it stand up in his season debut, fueling the host Columbus Blue Jackets to a 3-2 victory over the Pittsburgh Penguins on Friday.
All four games between the teams last season ventured past regulation before Friday's game followed suit.
Johnson scored by sending the puck between the pads of Sergei Murashov in the first round. Talbot denied Rickard Rakell and Ben Kindel in the first and third rounds, respectively, while former Blue Jacket Egor Chinakhov's attempt sailed wide of the net.
Columbus defenseman Damon Severson collected a goal and an assist in his season debut. He was activated from the injured/non-roster list after undergoing shoulder surgery in April.
Mathieu Olivier also scored and Cole Sillinger notched two assists for the Blue Jackets, who dictated play by enjoying a decisive advantage in both shots (45-22) and faceoff wins (30-15).
Talbot, who made 20 saves, was suiting up for his ninth NHL team after signing a one-year contract with Columbus on Sept. 14.
The well-rested Blue Jackets were playing in their first game since recording a 4-1 loss to the Utah Mammoth on Saturday.
Pittsburgh's Bryan Rust scored for the second time in as many games and Evgeni Malkin also tallied.
Murashov turned aside 43 shots for the Penguins, who have lost three in a row (0-2-1).
Despite being outshot 33-10 over the first two periods, Pittsburgh forged a 2-2 tie at 3:19 of the third. Malkin did the honors after backhanding home a loose puck following defenseman Erik Karlsson's shot from the point.
Defenseman Zach Werenski secured the attention of Pittsburgh's Rust and Rakell before wiring a cross-zone feed from the top of the right circle to Severson. He converted from the lower left circle to open the scoring at 10:52 of the first period.
Olivier doubled the advantage at 11:40 of the second period after his shot from the right circle caromed off both the post and the skate of Murashov before entering the net. The goal was the second of the season for Olivier.
Rust responded less than three minutes later by skating wide of Severson before tucking the puck past Talbot.
--Field Level Media

items.title: サッカー＝マンＣのマレスカ監督がクラブ擁護、「タイトルの価値に傷なし」
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［マンチェスター（英国）　９日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［マンチェスター（英国）　９日　ロイター］ - サッカーのイングランド・プレミアリーグ、マンチェスター・シティー（マンＣ）のエンツォ・マレスカ監督は９日、財務規定違反の問題を抱えている同クラブを擁護した。

マンＣは１１日に行われるプレミアリーグで、先月末に１００件以上の重大な財務規定違反を認定されて以降初の試合となる敵地でのリバプール戦を迎える。クラブはすべての不正行為を否定しており、１日に不服申し立てを行った。

ジョゼップ・グアルディオラ監督の下で３冠を達成した２０２２─２３シーズンにコーチ陣の一員だったマレスカ監督は、リバプール戦に向けた記者会見で、「当時、選手やクラブ、ペップ（グアルディオラ監督）がどれほど努力したか私はよく知っている。だから、その功績を疑う余地など全くない」と語った。また、功績に汚点があると感じるかと問われると、「全くない」と答えた。

６月にグアルディオラ監督の後任として指揮官に就任したマレスカ監督は、契約交渉中に財務規定違反の疑惑に関する話題が上がったことは一度もなかったと明かし、「私はクラブを信頼している。だからこそ、このクラブに加わった。ここ以外に自分がいたいと思うクラブもない。ここにいられることをとても嬉しく思っているし、就任した初日からずっと誇りに感じている」とコメント。就任前に今回の問題の展開を知っていたとしても、「間違いなく」監督職を引き受けていただろうと語った。

NEW DELHI: Central Delhi was sealed on Saturday (Oct 10), with thousands of police and paramilitaries on patrol, metro stations shut, mobile internet suspended and markets closed to guard against a youth protest demanding India's chief election officer quit.
The protest, called by the "Cockroach" youth movement, hopes to draw thousands of demonstrators who want Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to quit over a revision of voter lists that critics say favours Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party.
Touted by the organisers as a protest to "Save Democracy", it aims to be the biggest of the demonstrations that were launched last week after the Indian Express newspaper reported that Kumar's deputies had questioned and disagreed with him over the revision process that saw some 130 million voter names removed.
Opposition parties have long alleged that the government is trying to fix voter lists to its advantage and were quick to resurrect the allegations following the report.

Kumar has not commented but the Election Commission and the BJP have denied the allegations.
NEW CHALLENGE TO MODI The BJP says Modi's popularity and India's economic growth are some key reasons for its electoral dominance and that opposition parties are misleading the country as they are unable to win elections.
Nonetheless, the near daily protests by opposition groups pose a new political challenge to Modi, just months after similar demonstrations forced his education minister to quit over exam paper leaks.

Indian opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and his sister Priyanka Gandhi Vadra attend a protest organized by opposition parties demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, in New Delhi, India, Oct 7, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Adnan Abidi)

It also comes months before a series of key state elections starting in early 2027, including in the BJP-ruled most populous state of Uttar Pradesh.
The protesters, led by the self-named "Cockroach Janta Party", that began as an online satire, have said they will gather at Jantar Mantar - a site designated for protests by authorities in the heart of New Delhi - at 10 am. (0430 GMT).
FUNDAMENTAL RIGHT TO PROTEST, CJP SAYS Delhi Police said on Friday that they had not given permission for the protest as the request did not come on time, CJP had violated undertakings given during previous protests, and that authorities had to enforce the law and maintain peace.
Police also said protesters would face the force of the law if they violated the ban.
CJP leaders rejected the police decision and said they would go ahead with the protest as it was their fundamental right.
In what is seen as a bid to thwart protesters arriving in Delhi and the central business district where Jantar Mantar is located, several long-distance trains to the city were cancelled on Friday and 57 metro stations shut from Friday night.
Mobile internet services in a radius of 4 km (2.5 miles) of the protest area were ordered suspended from Friday night to Saturday night, ANI news agency reported citing a government order.

Not just a military theatre: Strategic significance of the Black Sea, beyond Russia & Ukraine

Royad Mammadov’s loss shows how naval conflict & commerce collide. It involved a Turkish shipowner, multinational crew, Ukrainian port, Romanian rescuers & an Italian destination.

Swasti Rao

10 October, 2026 07:30 am IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

The Royad Mammadov ship in the Black Sea after a fire aboard the vessel outside Romania's territorial waters left two people dead and prompted a rescue operation | Romanian Interior Ministry/Handout via REUTERS

Follow Us :

Text Size:
A-
A+

-->

New Delhi: The Black Sea has emerged as a major theatre in the Russian-Ukraine war, with events in that maritime region affecting the military balance on land, global food movement, and the security calculations of NATO states along its shores.

Its strategic importance comes from the fact that the Black Sea links Ukraine and Russia to Türkiye, southeastern Europe and, through two narrow straits, the Mediterranean.

What has now drawn the world’s attention is the spate of attacks and incidents involving commercial shipping in this crucial maritime corridor. On 5 October, a Turkish-owned vessel carrying corn caught fire and sank outside Romania’s territorial waters after leaving the Ukrainian port of Izmail. Romanian authorities reported two deaths and eleven people rescued. The Ukraine president blamed Russian drones for the attack.

Show Full Article

The next day, Bulgaria reported attacks involving two merchant ships in its exclusive economic zone. These incidents explain the importance of the Black Sea not just as a military theatre, but also as a gateway between Europe and the Mediterranean, and a working trade route on which civilian lives depend.

The four axes
The wider Russia–Ukraine war can be understood along four overlapping axes. First is the land battlefield, especially in eastern Ukraine’s Donbas. Second is the war of long-range strikes: Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries and other infrastructure, and Russia’s targeting of Ukrainian power systems, cities and civilians.

Third is the Black Sea, where the war’s nature changes because ports, shipping, missiles, aircraft and unmanned craft operate in one maritime space. A fourth, less direct dimension reaches parts of Africa where a proxy war is being played out between two sides.

What makes it an interesting case to study is that the imbalance at sea was striking in February 2022. One open-source count put Russia’s Black Sea Fleet at 275 vessels of all types, including 58 combat ships, or 74 combat units if patrol boats were counted. It had a missile cruiser, frigates, submarines and landing ships. Ukraine, on the contrary, had a small conventional navy, and its sole frigate was under repair.

By early 2026, Ukraine’s defence ministry estimated that around 30 percent of the Russian fleet’s combat assets were either destroyed or seriously damaged. That said, it is Ukraine’s assessment but it does capture the scale of a transformation which not many expected in 2022.

The significance of the Black Sea region is explained in six parts in the following sections.

Also Read: Ukraine’s robotic army is already at work. India must rethink the next battlefield

Geography & the food route
Apart from Ukraine and Russia, Georgia, Türkiye, Bulgaria, and Romania have a direct coastline along the Black Sea. To its southwest, ships pass through the Bosphorus, the Sea of Marmara and the Dardanelles into the Mediterranean.

To the northeast, the narrow Kerch Strait connects it with the Sea of Azov. Ports such as Odesa, Chornomorsk and Pivdennyi carry Ukrainian trade; Novorossiysk is a major Russian port. Its geography makes every port, chokepoint and shipping lane strategically consequential.

Crimea projects from the northern shore into the sea. Its position gives Sevastopol a sheltered naval base and helps whoever controls the Crimean peninsula or threaten much of the surrounding water.

Crimea’s history is deeper than a simplistic story of its ownership. Existing from 1441 to 1783, the Crimean Khanate preceded the annexation by the Russian Empire. The Soviet Union transferred Crimea to the Ukrainian republic in 1954. When Ukraine became independent in 1991, Crimea was within its internationally recognized borders.

Agreements in 1997 divided the former Soviet Black Sea Fleet and allowed Russia to base its fleet at Sevastopol under lease. Russia seized and annexed the peninsula in 2014; the United Nations and most of the countries did not recognize that change of status.

There is an older image that fixes Crimea in world history: the 1945 Yalta Conference that brought together US President Franklin D. Roosevelt, British Prime Minister Winston Churchill and Soviet leader Joseph Stalin to discuss the end of the Second World War.

Today, Crimea’s military significance is more immediate. Russia uses it for naval basing, air defence and logistics; Ukraine attacks it for that very reason The Kerch Bridge, opened after the annexation and connecting the peninsula to Russia, has become another target.

Then there is the food angle. Before the full-scale invasion, Ukraine supplied more than 45 million tonnes of grain per year to international markets, according to the UN Food and Agriculture Organisation.

Russia and Ukraine together accounted for roughly three tenths of global wheat exports before the war. The Black Sea is indispensable to the movement of their harvests. In 2021, 36 of 55 countries experiencing food crises obtained more than 10 percent of their wheat imports from Russia and Ukraine, and some obtained almost all of it. North African and Middle Eastern buyers are especially exposed, alongside other importers. A disruption to a port in Odesa or a ship near the Danube can, therefore, raise costs far beyond the battlefield.

How naval battle changed after 2022
In the beginning, Russia blockaded Ukrainian ports, used ships to support operations along the coast, and fired cruise missiles at Ukrainian targets. Ukraine responded with coastal missiles, mines, air and missile strikes, intelligence, and eventually explosive unmanned boats.

The first major turning point came in March and April 2022. Ukraine struck the Russian landing ship Saratov at occupied Berdiansk in March. In April, Neptune anti-ship missiles sank the Black Sea Fleet’s flagship, the Moskva. Russia said a fire and ammunition explosion preceded its loss.

The cruiser’s disappearance reduced air-defence cover at sea and had an enormous symbolic effect. In June, Russian forces withdrew from Snake Island after sustained attacks, loosening their hold over the northwestern Black Sea.

The next stage showed that Russian vessels were vulnerable even in harbour. In October 2022, Ukraine launched a combined aerial and unmanned surface-boat raid on Sevastopol. In 2023, strikes spread across the peninsula and farther east. A July attack damaged the Kerch Bridge.

In August, an explosive boat damaged the Olenegorsky Gornyak landing ship at Novorossiysk, showing that relocation could not guarantee safety. In September, missiles hit the landing ship Minsk and the Kalibr-capable submarine Rostov-on-Don in a Sevastopol dry dock. In December, a strike destroyed the Novocherkassk landing ship at Feodosia.

In early 2024, Ukrainian unmanned surface craft sank the missile corvette Ivanovets, the landing ship Kunikov and the patrol ship Sergey Kotov in separate attacks.

Russia dispersed valuable ships away from Sevastopol, especially towards Novorossiysk, and strengthened harbour defences. The result was a reduction in the fleet’s freedom to operate close to Ukraine’s coast, but not the disappearance of Russian naval power. Submarines, aircraft, coastal missiles and surviving surface vessels could still threaten Ukraine and shipping. Nevertheless, Ukraine achieved substantial sea denial without acquiring classic control of the entire Black Sea.

Türkiye, the Straits & the grain corridors
Türkiye occupies an unusual position. It is a NATO member, has supported Ukraine’s sovereignty and supplied it with weapons, yet has kept diplomatic and economic channels to Moscow open and hosted negotiations, including talks in Istanbul. It has tried to mediate rather than simply sever its relationship with either side. Its geography gives that balancing act practical weight: Türkiye controls the Bosphorus and Dardanelles Straits, the only passage between the Black Sea and the Mediterranean.

Under the 1936 Montreux Convention, merchant ships generally retain freedom of passage, while warships face restrictions. After the full-scale invasion, Türkiye applied the convention’s wartime provisions to restrict belligerent warships passing through the straits, subject to an exception for vessels returning to their home bases.

It also urged restraint by other states. The closure limited Russia’s ability to reinforce the Black Sea Fleet from its other fleets, while also constraining naval access more generally.

These rules also affect Russia’s wider military logistics. For years, the so-called Syrian Express (Russia’s military maritime logistics network) linked Russian ports with its military facilities at Tartus in Syria through the Turkish straits. Wartime restrictions complicated that naval route and required alternatives and longer logistical arrangements.

Türkiye and the UN brokered the Black Sea Grain Initiative in July 2022. It allowed inspected commercial ships to carry food from designated Ukrainian ports despite the war. Before Russia ended its participation in July 2023, the arrangement moved about 32.9 million tonnes of food to 45 countries. Russia argued its own agricultural exports faced obstacles; the initiative’s collapse exposed ports and merchants to renewed pressure.

Ukraine then established a new maritime route without the old inspection agreement. Ships leaving its Black Sea ports traveled westward along the coast and near the waters of NATO members Romania and Bulgaria before reaching the Turkish straits. The proximity to those states made the route more viable, and allies provided maritime security assistance and monitoring, but it was a Ukrainian-operated corridor, not a NATO guarantee or an EU-run convoy. Separately, the EU’s Solidarity Lanes carried Ukrainian goods through rail, road and Danube connections.

The volumes show that the corridor was more than a symbolic workaround. By February 2024, the British government said the new sea route had moved 19 million tonnes of cargo, including 13.4 million tonnes of agricultural goods. The European Commission reported that in July 2026 roughly 80 percent of Ukraine’s grain, oilseed and related-product exports traveled through Black Sea ports, compared with about 20 percent by the Solidarity Lanes.

Cumulatively from May 2022 to July 2026, it put those exports through Black Sea ports and the Solidarity Lanes at about 60 and 40 percent respectively, out of roughly 255 million tonnes. As the cumulative figures span both the original grain initiative and the later Ukrainian corridor, these numbers should not be credited entirely to the post-2023 route.

Also Read: India seeks safe Black Sea shipping, grain exports & non-attack understandings in Ukraine-Russia war

A contest of tech & adaptation
The innovation most associated with Ukraine’s naval campaign is the Magura V5: an unmanned surface vessel (USV) that can be used for kamikaze missions against warships and other targets. Another USV, the Sea Baby, has been used for longer-range strikes and other payloads. Their military value lies more in how they are used with reconnaissance, communications and coordinated attacks.

Ukraine has further transformed these USVs into a mobile launch platform. Missiles launched from unmanned boats have downed a Russian helicopter in 2024 and a fighter aircraft in 2025 . In late 2025, Ukraine claimed an underwater Sea Baby variant was used to strike a submarine in Novorossiysk. Russia disputed the claim.

Underwater capability may complicate harbour defence, but the precise damage in contested operations is harder to verify independently. Russia, in turn, has added barriers, patrols, electronic warfare and new defensive tactics, which goes on to show that this is an innovation race.

And then, there is a Turkish innovation as well. In November 2025, Turkish defence company Baykar said a Kızılelma unmanned combat aircraft used its radar to identify a jet-powered target and launched a Gökdoğan air-to-air missile in a successful test off the coast of Sinop over the Black Sea.

This showed how the Black Sea region has become a battle testing ground for unmanned air and maritime systems. Its relevance to the conflict is technological and geographic. The strategic effect is to change the price of movement.

A fleet that once assumed it could approach Ukraine’s shore has had to spend more effort protecting ships, bases and logistics. Ukraine still cannot make the sea safe simply by pushing warships back. Mines, missile and drone attacks on ports, and threats to civilian vessels persist.

Why the story remains unfinished
The 5 October loss of cargo ship Royad Mammadov shows how the naval and commercial stories meet. A Turkish owner, a multinational crew, a Ukrainian port call, Romanian rescue services and a destination in Italy were all involved in one voyage.

Ukraine attributed the incident to Russian drones; independent findings on its cause were not yet established in the Romanian account. Bulgaria’s report of two merchant ships attacked the following day added to concern that danger was spreading into waters where NATO coastal states have rescue and security responsibilities. An incident in an exclusive economic zone can still have serious human and diplomatic consequences.

There is an economic cost even when ships continue sailing. Reuters reported Ukrainian grain exports in September 2026 were 36.6 percent lower than a year earlier, a figure that should not be attributed to naval attacks alone because harvests, demand and logistics all these factors also affect exports. However, It is an indication of why a functioning maritime corridor needs constant attention.

A regional war with global consequences
So the ready reckoner is this. Russia began the full-scale war with the dominant conventional fleet. Ukraine used missiles, unmanned systems and repeated strikes to deny that fleet easy use of the northwestern sea and its Crimean base.

Türkiye’s control of the straits limits naval reinforcement while allowing commercial passage under different rules. Ukraine rebuilt a route for its exports after the grain deal ended, and the sea remains central to food supplies abroad.

Yet neither side has made it a safe or settled maritime space. The most revealing question now is not simply how many Russian warships Ukraine has sunk but whether civilians, cargoes and coastal states can continue to use the Black Sea while a war is being fought across it.

Other navies are studying how inexpensive unmanned craft, shore-based missiles and air defence systems can constrain larger fleets. For the region, the stakes extend from Crimea and the Ukrainian coast through Türkiye’s straits into Mediterranean security and Russian logistics.

The global stake is more immediate for many households: ships carrying wheat, corn and sunflower oil link these shores to food prices and supply chains in North Africa, the Middle East, Asia and elsewhere.

And, then there is an India hook because it illustrates that wider reach. Reuters reported on 7 October that a 20,000-tonne cargo of Russian sunflower oil bound for India was cancelled after damage to Black Sea port infrastructure, while about 60,000 tonnes faced delays.

Reports also indicate that India has offered ideas on energy infrastructure and safe shipping, and Foreign Minister S. Jaishankar has held conversations with Moscow and Kyiv. The details and prospects of any Indian mediation are still uncertain.

But, a serious effort to protect commercial shipping and reduce attacks in Black Sea would answer a concern shared by many developing countries, whose interest is reliable food and energy supplies.

(Edited by Tony Rai)

items.title: Frederick Gaudreau scores twice as Kraken separate from Red Wings
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Frederick Gaudreau scored two of Seattle's four straight second-period goals as the Kraken pulled away to a 6-3 victory over the host Detroit Red Wings on Friday.
items.body:
Frederick Gaudreau scored two of Seattle's four straight second-period goals as the Kraken pulled away to a 6-3 victory over the host Detroit Red Wings on Friday.
Ben Meyers supplied a goal and two assists, while Berkly Catton had a goal and an assist. Mackie Samoskevich and Vince Dunn also scored for the Kraken, while Philipp Grubauer made 37 saves.
William Wallinder and Michael Brandsegg-Nygard scored their first NHL goals for Detroit. Viktor Arvidsson scored for the third straight game.
The Red Wings had a 16-5 shots on goal advantage in the first period but it ended in a 1-1 tie.
With Jordan Eberle in the penalty box for slashing, the Red Wings scored at 9:19 of the period. Lucas Raymond took a shot from the right side that trickled through the legs of Grubauer. Arvidsson then tapped it into the net.
Catton tied it with 5:08 left in the period. He took a pass from Kaapo Kakko and pushed a backhander past Detroit starting goalie John Gibson on the short side. Josh Mahura picked up the second assist.
Wallinder scored his breakthrough with a shot from the point four minutes into the second period. Alex DeBrincat and Brandsegg-Nygård collected the assists.
Gaudreau scored 39 seconds later to tie it. He converted from short range off a behind-the-net pass from Ryan Winterton. Meyers had the second assist.
Samoskevich gave the Kraken the lead at 6:59 of the period. He scored in front off a feed from Jared McCann.
Gaudreau's second goal of the game came at 7:44 of the period. He lifted a shot over Gibson's glove from the left circle. Winterton and Meyers once again had the assists.
Meyers made it 5-2 with 5:55 left in the period with assists from Catton and Brandon Montour. Right after serving a penalty, Meyers skated into the offensive zone and fired a shot from the right circle past Gibson.
That ended Gibson's night, as he was pulled for Daniil Tarasov.
Dunn scored during a 5-on-3 advantage in the third period.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Capitals prevail after Rangers lose G Igor Shesterkin to injury
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Boone Jenner scored the tiebreaking goal late in the second period and the host Washington Capitals won 3-1 on Friday, cooling off the New York Rangers, who lost star goaltender Igor Shesterkin to a lower-body injury.
items.body:
Boone Jenner scored the tiebreaking goal late in the second period and the host Washington Capitals won 3-1 on Friday, cooling off the New York Rangers, who lost star goaltender Igor Shesterkin to a lower-body injury.
Timothy Liljegren also scored, Tom Wilson added an empty-netter and Logan Thompson made 22 saves for Washington, which has won three of its first four on the season. The Capitals also snapped the Rangers' four-game winning streak.
Shesterkin, who entered with a 3-1-0 record, a 1.75 goals-against average and a .926 save percentage this season, appeared to awkwardly jam his right skate into the goalpost while sliding into position to make a save with 11:40 remaining in the second period of a 1-1 contest.
The former Vezina Trophy winner, who stopped 13 of the 14 shots he saw on Friday, remained down on the ice for several minutes and had to be helped to the bench by a pair of teammates. Backup Dylan Garand, who made 22 saves in New York's 2-0 win at Detroit on Oct. 2, replaced Shesterkin and stopped 11 of 12 shots.
As Garand manned the Rangers' net, Washington took the lead with 2:22 left in the middle frame via a turnover in the New York zone. Jenner intercepted the ill-advised pass from Rangers star Adam Fox in the slot, and he converted a snap shot for his first goal as a Capital.
After recording a hat trick in the Rangers' 5-2 win over the rival New York Islanders on Tuesday, Alexis Lafreniere opened the scoring with 9:43 remaining in the first period on a power play. Skating into the high slot, Lafreniere worked for enough of an opening to beat a seemingly off-balance Thompson.
Washington tied it 6:08 into the second period. Liljegren hammered a point shot that found its way past a screened Shesterkin.
Capitals superstar Alex Ovechkin, the league's all-time leader with 929 goals and playing in his 22nd and final NHL season, recorded two shots on goal but remained goalless on the campaign.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Isaias weakens to Category 1 hurricane after Florida landfall, NHC says
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Nearly 380,000 people in Florida and more than 210,000 in Alabama were left without power as the storm hit shore.
items.body:
Hurricane Isaias rapidly lost windspeed on Friday, weakening into a Category 1 event after making landfall near Destin, Florida, the US National Hurricane Center said, but warned of danger from storm surges and floods as power links snapped.
The hurricane was about 65 miles (105 km) west-northwest of Panama City, Florida, packing maximum sustained winds of 90 mph (150 kph), the NHC said in its most recent advisory.
The agency warned against a life-threatening storm surge affecting the Gulf Coast as dangerous hurricane conditions and flash floods spread inland.
The hurricane is expected to cross Alabama and into the Tennessee Valley on the weekend, the agency added.
Nearly 380,000 people in Florida and more than 210,000 in Alabama were left without power as the storm hit shore, the website Poweroutage.us showed.
"Emergency declarations have been approved in Florida and Alabama to ensure federal resources are available to respond to Isaias," Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said on X.
Florida's emergency services urged residents to shelter in place and watch for hurricane conditions across the state's north after Isaias hit land as a category 2 storm.

items.title: Trump estime que la Norvège porte une "tache indélébile" pour ne pas lui avoir décerné le prix Nobel de la paix
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Le président américain Donald Trump s'est plaint amèrement vendredi de ne pas avoir reçu le prix Nobel de la paix, estimant que cette décision avait jeté une tache sur la Norvège.
items.body:
Le président américain Donald Trump s'est plaint amèrement vendredi de ne pas avoir reçu le prix Nobel de la paix, estimant que cette décision avait jeté une tache sur la Norvège.
Navanethem "Navi" Pillay, ancienne juge de la Cour pénale internationale (CPI), qui a supervisé une enquête de l'Onu ayant conclu qu'Israël avait commis un génocide à Gaza, a remporté vendredi le [USN:L8N45V0JP TEXT:"prix Nobel de la paix"] pour "ses efforts en faveur de la paix et du droit international".
Donald Trump a estimé que Navi Pillay était une "inconnue" lors d'un rassemblement à Syracuse, dans l'Etat de New York, organisé en amont des élections de mi-mandat aux Etats-Unis. "Je n'ai jamais entendu parler de cette personne. Personne n'en a entendu parler."
"Il s'agit d'une tache indélébile pour la Norvège et pour ces gens qui ont pris une décision si honteuse et embarrassante", a dit le locataire de la Maison blanche.
"Le prix Nobel de la paix a été discrédité pour toujours par une poignée d'idéologues radicaux, hostiles à la démocratie et véritables ennemis de la civilisation. Nous n'oublierons pas, Norvège", a dit Donald Trump.
Le prix Nobel de la paix est remis à Oslo, en Norvège.
L'administration américaine a annoncé, quelques heures après que Navi Pillay a reçu le prix, des [USN:L8N45V1HE TEXT:"sanctions"] visant à paralyser le fonctionnement de la Cour pénale internationale (CPI).

items.title: Trump says Norway has 'indelible stain' for not awarding him Nobel Peace Prize
items.author: Jacob Bogage
items.creator: Jacob Bogage
items.summary: Each year of his presidency, Trump has expressed disappointment at his failure to win the prize.
items.body:
US President Donald Trump reiterated his complaints on Friday about not receiving the Nobel Peace Prize, calling it a disgraceful and embarrassing decision that had left a stain on Norway, which hosts the Nobel committee.
Trump unleashed on Norway hours after the committee awarded this year's prize to [USN:L8N45V0JG TEXT:"Navi Pillay,"] a former International Criminal Court judge who oversaw a UN report that concluded Israel committed genocide in Gaza.
Trump called Pillay a "mystery person" during a campaign rally in Syracuse, New York. "I never heard of the person. Nobody did."
Each year of his presidency, Trump has expressed disappointment at his failure to win the prize.
"This is an indelible stain on the country of Norway and those people that made such a disgraceful and embarrassing decision," Trump said.
He listed a number of conflicts that he [USN:L1N3UC0RP TEXT:"claimed a role in resolving"] and said he has helped prevent wars from breaking out between North and South Korea, Japan and North Korea, and China and Taiwan, without providing evidence.
"The Nobel Peace Prize has been forever discredited by a handful of radical ideologues who are anti-democracy and really enemies of civilization. And we will not forget, Norway," he said.

items.title: Mulino recorre zonas afectadas por el terremoto en Panamá y ordena medidas preventivas
items.author: Carolina Pulice, Lauren Rosenthal
items.summary: El sismo de magnitud 7,7 sacudió la provincia de Herrera, a más de 193 kilómetros al suroeste del Canal de Panamá, según el Servicio Geológico de Estados Unidos (USGS).
items.body: Bloomberg — Panamá fue sacudida el viernes por el terremoto más fuerte en más de siete décadas, seguido de potentes réplicas, mientras que el presidente José Raúl Mulino declaró que no se habían reportado muertes inmediatamente después del sismo. El sismo de magnitud 7,7 sacudió la provincia de Herrera, a más de 193 kilómetros al suroeste del Canal de Panamá, según el Servicio Geológico de Estados Unidos (USGS). Las pérdidas económicas en la región podrían superar los US$1.000 millones, según una estimación preliminar del USGS. Según el Centro Nacional de Información Sismológica de Estados Unidos, el terremoto fue el más fuerte que ha azotado esa zona de Panamá desde al menos 1951. El Servicio Geológico de Estados Unidos (USGS) indicó que tuvo lugar a una profundidad de 12,6 kilómetros. Ver más: Sismo de 7,2 sacude a Panamá: el canal opera con normalidad y el aeropuerto de Tocumen está cerrado Según las lecturas preliminares del USGS, una réplica de magnitud 6,6 se registró al oeste del epicentro del terremoto inicial a última hora de la tarde del viernes. Además, se han registrado otras ocho réplicas de magnitud 4,8 o superior. El primer terremoto fue causado por una ruptura a lo largo del límite de una placa principal en el Cinturón de Fuego, la zona sísmicamente activa que rodea el Océano Pacífico. El mecanismo se asemejó a un deslizamiento horizontal, en el que las placas tectónicas se rozan entre sí, según Jonathan Tytell, geofísico del Centro Nacional de Información sobre Terremotos de Estados Unidos. “Fue un evento muy caótico y superficial, lo cual no es bueno”, dijo Tytell. “La energía está ahí mismo, en la superficie, y no tiene tiempo ni distancia para disiparse”. El Servicio Geológico de Estados Unidos (USGS) registró inicialmente una magnitud de 8.0 antes de revisarla. El instituto geológico de Panamá informó que el terremoto tuvo una magnitud de 7.2. Inmediatamente después del terremoto, el Centro de Alerta de Tsunamis del Pacífico indicó que eran posibles olas de entre uno y tres metros (3,3 a 9,8 pies) por encima del nivel de la marea en algunas zonas de la costa panameña. A las 14:42 hora local, se levantaron todas las alertas. El Canal de Panamá informó que las operaciones continuaban con normalidad, con los protocolos de emergencia activados y equipos técnicos inspeccionando las instalaciones en busca de posibles daños. Ver más: Panamá sale de la lista negra de la UE tras seis años y estos son los ocho países que siguen Según medios locales, el sismo se sintió incluso en varias ciudades colombianas, incluida Medellín. En Panamá, la población evacuó edificios, negocios, escuelas y viviendas en diversas regiones, informó el diario local La Prensa. El Aeropuerto Internacional de Tocumen, en Panamá, permaneció cerrado tras el terremoto, pero posteriormente reabrió sus puertas. Mulino declaró que el gobierno estaba movilizando personal, recursos y ayuda para las personas afectadas por el terremoto, y ordenó a los ministerios y organismos públicos que respondieran de inmediato y tomaran medidas preventivas. Se esperaba que los funcionarios de emergencia ofrecieran una rueda de prensa para informar sobre el impacto del sismo. Durante su recorrido por la zona afectada el viernes, Mulino declaró a la prensa que se estaban realizando esfuerzos para reubicar a las familias que vivían en viviendas dañadas. Asimismo, se estaba analizando la posibilidad de trasladar a los pacientes de los hospitales afectados. El ministro de Hacienda de Panamá, Felipe Chapman, afirmó que se había puesto en contacto con el Banco Mundial, el Fondo Monetario Internacional y otros bancos “para obtener los recursos necesarios para hacer frente a esta crisis”. La Corporación Andina de Fomento, conocida como CAF, una de las instituciones contactadas, anunció que donaría US$250.000 a Panamá para la ayuda tras el terremoto. Mulino agradeció a la CAF su “rápida ayuda”. La gente permanecía descalza o sin camiseta en las calles mientras continuaban las réplicas, según explicó Cibeles De Freitas, responsable de comunicación de la filial local de First Quantum Minerals Ltd. “Hay mucho miedo porque en Panamá no estamos acostumbrados a los terremotos”, afirmó. “Estamos bien, pero muy asustados”. First Quantum Minerals comunicó en las redes sociales que la infraestructura de Cobre Panamá, su mina de cobre parcialmente inactiva, situada a unos 140 kilómetros al norte del epicentro, se mantenía estable y segura tras el terremoto. El Metro de la ciudad de Panamá informó de que las líneas 1 y 2 se cerraron temporalmente a causa del terremoto. El cuerpo de bomberos de Panamá indicó que no se habían registrado víctimas mortales ni heridos inmediatamente después del sismo. AES Panamá, una filial de AES Corp., el principal proveedor de electricidad del país, declaró a través de un portavoz que sus centrales hidroeléctricas, de gas y de energías renovables seguían operativas. Ver más: Tráfico por el estrecho de Magallanes se dispara más de 70% mientras buques evitan el Canal de Panamá Las actividades en el oleoducto Transpanamá continuaban con normalidad tras el sismo, según un comunicado de su operador. El terremoto del viernes ha sido el último que ha sacudido América Latina en los últimos meses. A finales de junio, Venezuela sufrió dos terremotos consecutivos que causaron la muerte de casi 6.500 personas y provocaron una destrucción generalizada a lo largo de su costa norte. En Colombia, un terremoto ocurrido el 10 de agosto se cobró la vida de más de 330 personas y provocó una emergencia económica, ya que los daños se estimaron en aproximadamente US$10.000 millones. La presidenta interina de Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez, ofreció asistencia a Panamá, al igual que el presidente colombiano, Abelardo de la Espriella. “Panamá no está sola”, dijo De la Espriella en una publicación en X, y agregó que Colombia estaba lista para brindar toda la ayuda necesaria. El secretario de Estado estadounidense, Marco Rubio, dijo en una publicación en redes sociales que estaba siguiendo de cerca la situación y agregó que “el Departamento de Estado está movilizando rápidamente recursos y personal para brindar asistencia”. --Con la colaboración de James Attwood, Valentine Hilaire, José Orozco, Brian K. Sullivan, Michael McDonald, Lucía Kassai y Sarah Gray. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

items.title: Rangers G Igor Shesterkin exits vs. Capitals with lower-body injury
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: New York Rangers goaltender Igor Shesterkin exited in the second period against the host Washington Capitals with a lower-body injury Friday night and did not return.
items.body:
New York Rangers goaltender Igor Shesterkin exited in the second period against the host Washington Capitals with a lower-body injury Friday night and did not return.
Shesterkin, who entered the contest with a 3-1-0 record and 1.75 goals-against average on the young season, appeared to awkwardly jam his right skate into the goalpost while sliding into position to make a save with 11:40 remaining in the middle frame of a 1-1 game. He was helped off the ice without putting any pressure on his right leg.
"Well, it's concerning, obviously," said Rangers coach Mike Sullivan, who didn't have any update on Shesterkin's status after the game. "He's an elite goaltender, and you don't ever want to see anybody get hurt, but, obviously, he's an important player for us."
The Rangers ended up losing 3-1 to the Capitals.
Shesterkin, a former Vezina Trophy winner who stopped 13 of the 14 shots he saw Friday, remained down on the ice for several minutes and had to be helped to the bench by a pair of teammates. Backup Dylan Garand, who made 22 saves in New York's 2-0 win at Detroit on Oct. 2, replaced Shesterkin.
Garand finished with 11 saves on 12 shots.
"It's awful. He's a pillar of this team," Rangers captain J.T. Miller said of Shesterkin getting hurt. "It stinks. ... We don't even know what's going on, but to see him leave the game is a shot to all of us, a shock to all of us. But at the same time, it means we got to step up to a man to try to get the job done, especially (Garand)."
The Rangers had their four-game winning streak snapped.
--Field Level Media

items.title: サッカー＝監視対象の選手・関係者の過半数が誹謗中傷受信、ＦＩＦＡ発表
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［９日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［９日　ロイター］ - 国際サッカー連盟（ＦＩＦＡ）は９日、２０２６年ワールドカップ（Ｗ杯）北中米３カ国大会においてソーシャルメディア保護サービス（ＳＭＰＳ）によって監視された選手、監督、関係者の計１６０６人のうち、半数以上がオンライン上で誹謗中傷を受けていたと発表した。

監視対象となった１６０６人のうち８１２人が、誹謗中傷と分類されるメッセージを少なくとも１件受信した。差別的な誹謗中傷の中で最も多かったのは人種差別に関するもので、誹謗中傷全体の１２％を占めた。一般的な誹謗中傷を除くと、その割合は２０％に上った。

最も標的とされた特定の個人は１万件以上の誹謗中傷投稿を受け取り、そのうち４０％が人種差別的な内容だった。

ＳＭＰＳは１７１０万件の投稿やコメントを分析し、そのうち約２４万件が人の目による精査を経て誹謗中傷であると確認された。２９０５のアカウントについて調査が必要と判断され、７８６アカウントが審査のため法執行機関に報告された。

投稿監視ツールは、ＦＩＦＡおよび加盟協会の公式チャンネルにおける６０７０万件のコメントをスキャンし、スパムを含め９２０万件を非表示にした。

items.title: US says Chinese actions off Taiwan are 'deeply destabilising'
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: China's maritime actions off Taiwan's east coast are "deeply destabilising" and only worsen tension, the US State Department said, after Reuters reported the first known sighting of a Chinese militia boat in those waters in August.
items.body:
China's maritime actions off Taiwan's east coast are "deeply destabilising" and only worsen tension, the US State Department said, after Reuters reported the first known sighting of a Chinese [USN:L4N45S05G TEXT:"militia boat"] in those waters in August.
China, which views Taiwan as its own territory, has stepped up activity off the island's [USN:L1N42902N TEXT:"east coast"] since June with regular coast guard patrols.
Officials in Taiwan, which rejects Beijing's sovereignty claims, say they believe China is practicing for a possible maritime blockade using overlapping military, paramilitary and civilian assets.
Taipei regards the area off its east coast as critical to wartime supply routes from allies in the event of a blockade or conflict.
The United States remains concerned by China's activity east of Taiwan, a State Department spokesperson said, responding to a question on the sighting of the militia boat.
"China's actions are deeply destabilising," the spokesperson added.
"By asserting authorities around maritime areas that Taiwan has peacefully administered for over 70 years, China only exacerbates tensions and undermines the peaceful resolution of issues that it claims to seek."
The United States urges Beijing to cease its pressure against Taiwan and instead engage in "meaningful dialogue with Taiwan's democratically elected authorities", the spokesperson added.
China's foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment. China recognises no claims of sovereignty by Taiwan, including over waters surrounding it.
The United States is Taiwan's most important international backer, though President Donald Trump has yet to approve a new [USN:L4N45S03H TEXT:"$14 billion"] arms sale package for the island.
Taiwan's Coast Guard said in a statement about the militia boat and its accompanying vessels that their activities were all located outside of "restricted waters".
In a practice dating to the 1950s, China's maritime militia, more commonly seen around [USN:L6N43M0E3 TEXT:"South China Sea"] flashpoints, consists of fishing vessels whose crews receive training and support to operate in disputed waters, often alongside coast guard ships.
In June, Britain, France, Germany and the United States, all expressed [USN:L1N42W093 TEXT:"concern"] over Chinese activities off Taiwan's east coast as a threat to regional stability and freedom of navigation.

items.title: ＭＬＢ＝ドジャース山本、リーグ優勝決定Ｓ第2戦で先発へ　初戦はスクバル
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［９日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［９日　ロイター］ - 米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）ドジャースのデーブ・ロバーツ監督は９日、ブルワーズとのナ・リーグ優勝決定シリーズ（７回戦制）で、１１日の第１戦にタリク・スクバル投手、１２日の第２戦に山本由伸投手を先発させると明らかにした。ＭＬＢ公式サイトが伝えた。

ドジャースはブレーブスとの地区シリーズを３勝１敗で突破。先発したスクバル、ブレーク・スネル、山本、タイラー・グラスノーの４投手は計２１回１／３を投げて自責４、防御率１．６９を記録した。今季のプレーオフ出場チームではレイズの先発陣に次ぐ２番目の好成績となっている。

地区シリーズで第３戦に先発した山本は７回を４安打１失点、１四球、１０三振と好投。中５日で第２戦に登板する予定で、シリーズが第６戦までもつれた場合も通常の登板間隔で先発できる見込み。

山本は昨年のワールドシリーズで最優秀選手（ＭＶＰ）に選出され、最終第７戦では前日の登板から休養なしで救援登板した。今季のプレーオフでも短い登板間隔や救援での起用に応じる意向を示しているが、球団は可能な限り通常の登板間隔を維持する方針。

スネルがリーグ優勝決定シリーズ第３戦、グラスノーが第４戦に先発する可能性がある。ドジャースは昨年まで２年連続でワールドシリーズを制しており、３連覇を目指す。

items.title: Petroecuador levanta la declaratoria de fuerza mayor en una estación de bombeo del oleoducto SOTE
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: La petrolera estatal ecuatoriana Petroecuador dijo el viernes que levantó la declaratoria de fuerza mayor en una estación de bombeo del oleoducto SOTE y recuperó su capacidad de transporte a un flujo de 312.000 barriles por día.
items.body:
La petrolera estatal ecuatoriana Petroecuador dijo el viernes que levantó la declaratoria de fuerza mayor en una estación de bombeo del oleoducto SOTE y recuperó su capacidad de transporte a un flujo de 312.000 barriles por día.
La empresa había reanudado el bombeo a través del oleoducto el jueves, tras un incendio ocurrido a inicio de mes, que afectó a la estación de bombeo de Baeza y obligó a declarar la fuerza mayor en esa infraestructura.
Petroecuador dijo en un comunicado que la víspera fue recuperada la sexta unidad de bombeo de la estación Baeza, permitiendo incrementar el transporte del crudo. La capacidad de transporte del SOTE es de 360.000 barriles por día (bpd).
"El levantamiento de la fuerza mayor marca el retorno a la operación normal del sistema de oleoductos y posibilita la continuidad de los procesos de exploración, producción, refinación, comercialización nacional y entrega de crudo al mercado internacional", agregó la petrolera en un comunicado.

items.title: Boca Juniors empata en su visita a Instituto en liga argentina
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Boca Juniors igualó el viernes 2-2 en su visita a Instituto de Córdoba en el inicio de la duodécima jornada del torneo Clausura del fútbol argentino.
items.body:
Boca Juniors igualó el viernes 2-2 en su visita a Instituto de Córdoba en el inicio de la duodécima jornada del torneo Clausura del fútbol argentino.
Instituto mantuvo el liderato en la Zona A con 26 puntos en la tabla de posiciones, mientras que Boca quedó escolta con 21.
En el partido disputado en el estadio Mario Kempes de la provincia de Córdoba, "La Gloria" abrió el marcador a los 14 minutos con un remate de Fernando Alarcón.
Nueve minutos después, Boca Juniors empató por intermedio del ecuatoriano Enner Valencia tras una salida en falso del portero Marcos Ledesma.
En el inicio del segundo tiempo, Instituto volvió a sacar ventaja a los 48 minutos con un gol de Jonathan Galván, mientras que Boca logró la igualada a los 56 gracias al uruguayo Miguel Merentiel.
"Es un punto bueno ante un rival de jerarquía. Creíamos que lo podíamos ganar, pero nos terminan empatando dos veces", dijo Galván tras el empate.
En otros partidos del viernes, Sarmiento venció 3-1 como visitante a Aldosivi de Mar del Plata, mientras que Gimnasia y Esgrima La Plata y Atlético Tucumán empataron 1-1.

items.title: Ｆ１＝シンガポールＧＰスプリント予選、フェルスタッペンがトップ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［シンガポール　９日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［シンガポール　９日　ロイター］ - 自動車レースＦ１の第１７戦、シンガポール・グランプリ（ＧＰ）は９日、スプリント予選を行い、レッドブルのマックス・フェルスタッペン（オランダ）がトップタイムを記録した。

フェルスタッペンは１分３１秒１５６をマークし、２番手のジョージ・ラッセル（英国、メルセデス）に０秒１２０差をつけた。シンガポールでは過去に、ポールポジション（ＰＰ）獲得も優勝もともに経験していなかった。

フェルスタッペンは「ソフトタイヤを装着すると、マシンが少し生き返ったように感じた。トップになれるとは予想していなかったので、とてもうれしい」とコメントした。

３番手はシャルル・ルクレール（モナコ、フェラーリ）。総合首位のキミ・アントネッリ（イタリア、メルセデス）は７番手だった。

ラッセルは同日のフリー走行でトップタイムを記録したが、パワーユニットの部品交換に伴い、１１日の決勝では計４０グリッド降格のペナルティーを受ける。ただ、１０日のスプリントには影響しない。

スプリント予選の最初のセッションでは、セルヒオ・ペレス（メキシコ、キャデラック）が防護壁に衝突し、コース上に破片が散乱したため赤旗中断となった。その後、計時システムの不具合で第２セッションの開始が遅れたほか、追い抜き支援機能の作動にも問題が発生した。

items.title: Winless Kings head on the road to face Golden Knights
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Still in search of their first win in the Peter Laviolette era, the Los Angeles Kings make the short trip to Las Vegas to face the defending Western Conference champion Vegas Golden Knights on Saturday night.
items.body:
Still in search of their first win in the Peter Laviolette era, the Los Angeles Kings make the short trip to Las Vegas to face the defending Western Conference champion Vegas Golden Knights on Saturday night.
Los Angeles is 0-2-1 in its first three games under Laviolette, including road losses at Colorado (8-4) and San Jose (5-4 in OT). They come in off a 2-1 loss to the Florida Panthers on Tuesday in their home opener.
Despite the slow start, the Kings, just one point ahead of winless Calgary at the bottom of the Pacific Division, remain optimistic about what lies ahead.
"I'm just excited for us to put a full 60 minutes together," veteran Kings defenseman Joel Edmundson said. "I think we'll be a fun team to watch, a hard team to play against. We just haven't been able to get that full 60 (minutes) yet, but every day we're getting better and better."
Captain Drew Doughty said it doesn't feel like his team is as bad as its record so far.
"The first one (at Colorado) is the only one that feels like that," Doughty said. "San Jose, we shot ourselves in the foot. I thought we could have won that one."
The Kings finished with 27 giveaways in the sloppy loss to the Panthers.
"We just made more mistakes to give them opportunities than they did," Doughty said. "I don't think we need to adjust anything on systems. I just think we need to do them better, and when we get our chances, we've got to capitalize."
Los Angeles will have to do it without forward Mats Zuccarello for the near future. Laviolette announced after practice Friday that Zuccarello would not make the trip to Las Vegas and is "week-to-week" with an undisclosed injury. Forward Jared Wright was recalled from AHL affiliate Ontario to take his place on the roster.
Vegas comes in off a 4-3 shootout victory over the Toronto Maple Leafs on Thursday, rallying from a 3-0 first-period deficit in the process.
Jack Eichel continued his hot start with a penalty-shot goal and an assist, Adin Hill made 21 saves and snapped a seven-game losing streak in shootouts, and 20-year-old rookie forward Trevor Connelly scored the winner in the fifth round of the shootout with a nifty move and backhand goal around the left pad of Sergei Bobrovsky.
"I've been practicing a bit at the end of practice," Connelly said. "I knew I had a couple of moves that I thought would work. I just trusted my instincts and luckily it went in."
It marked just the fifth time in team history that the Golden Knights rallied from a three-goal deficit to pick up a win.
"I just think it shows how resilient we are, how up and down the lineup everyone is going to have an impact," Connelly said. "When we get down, we're not giving up."
"I liked that we picked each other up," Vegas coach Ryan Craig added. "I liked that we stayed with it individually and as a team. I don't like going down 3-0, but there's something to be said with how we stuck together."
--Field Level Media

items.title: India detains protesters, locks down Delhi ahead of rally against election chief
items.author: Saurabh Sharma, Aftab Ahmed, Sakshi Dayal
items.creator: Saurabh Sharma, Aftab Ahmed, Sakshi Dayal
items.summary: With metro stations and markets shut and mobile internet suspended, police boarded buses to check for protesters, witnesses said.
items.body:
Police in the Indian capital detained scores of protesters on Saturday amid patrols by [USN:L1N45V075 TEXT:"thousands of security forces"], with travel and telecoms links suspended, in a lockdown to stop a youth protest asking the election chief to quit.
The protest by the "Cockroach" youth movement, aims to draw thousands of demonstrators against Chief Election Commissioner [USN:L4N45K0DB TEXT:"Gyanesh Kumar"] over a [USN:L1N45V037 TEXT:"revision of voter lists"] that critics say favours Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party.
Television images showed police in the central business district of New Delhi chasing down a few dozen young protesters, some wearing backpacks, before they were loaded into vehicles and hauled away.
About 200 protesters were detained in the area, a police source told Reuters. Those detained outside Delhi included protest supporter Dhruv Rathee, a popular figure on YouTube, a police spokesperson said.
With metro stations and markets shut and mobile internet suspended, police boarded buses to check for protesters after stopping them at points of entry into the city, with cars and other vehicles also subjected to checks, Reuters witnesses said.
Barricades and concrete blocks stopped traffic, while anti-riot vehicles mounted with tear gas guns were stationed on key routes, they said.
"Why is the prime minister so scared of the country's youth, the country's people?" Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the self-named 'Cockroach Janta Party' that called the protest, asked on Saturday, shortly before leaving for Delhi.
"Why did you need to close all the railways, the metro, the internet has been closed, roads have been closed? ... this is nothing but fear," he told the ANI news agency in the financial capital of Mumbai.
The protesters have said they plan to gather at Jantar Mantar, a protest site designated by authorities in the heart of New Delhi, at 10 a.m.
NEW CHALLENGE TO MODI The protest, touted by the CJP as an effort to "Save Democracy", is planned as the biggest of a series of demonstrations launched last week after the Indian Express newspaper said Kumar's deputies had queried and disagreed with him over list revisions that dropped about 130 million voters.
That number exceeds the population of Japan.
Opposition parties have long accused the government of trying to fix voter lists to its advantage and were quick to resurrect the allegations following the report.
Kumar has not commented but the Election Commission and the BJP have denied the allegations.
The BJP says Modi's popularity and India's economic growth are key reasons for its electoral dominance and accuses opposition parties of misleading the country as they are unable to win elections.
Nonetheless, the near [USN:L6N45U0IF TEXT:"daily protests"] by opposition groups pose a new political challenge to Modi, just months after similar demonstrations forced his [USN:L1N43R02E TEXT:"education minister to quit"] over exam paper leaks.
They also come months before a series of key state elections starting in early 2027, among them one in the most populous state of Uttar Pradesh, ruled by the BJP.
On Friday, Delhi police said they had not given permission for the protest and violators would face the force of the law.
Their "temporary and precautionary" curbs aimed at regulating people's movement, preventing overcrowding, maintaining public order, and ensuring the safety of protesters and others in the affected areas, police said in a statement.
CJP leaders rejected the police decision and said they would go ahead with the protest as it was their fundamental right.
DELETIONS AFFECTED STATE POLLS, OPPOSITION ALLEGES The protesters accuse the BJP of using the revision of voter lists to sway election results, in collusion with its appointees in the Election Commission, including Kumar.
Opposition parties say the voter deletions affected the outcome of some recent state elections won by the BJP, and have cast a shadow on the electoral process in the world's largest democracy.
Election Commission data, also cited by the BJP, shows about 130 million names, have been deleted from voter lists during the verification exercise, including 63 million who relocated, 30 million who could not be traced, and 28 million dead.
The commission says the count represents voter entries flagged during the draft revision stage, that the exercise is not complete yet, and voters wrongly removed can enroll again.

items.title: U.S. Expands African Critical Minerals Investments in Africa to Challenge China’s Dominance
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: By Olivia Kumwenda-Mtambo The U.S. International Development Finance Corp plans to increase direct equity investments, including in Africa and the critical minerals sector, the agency’s Africa head said, as the U.S. steps up efforts to counter China’s dominance of key supply chains. …
items.summary_source: The China-Global South Project source metadata
items.body:
By Olivia Kumwenda-Mtambo

The U.S. International Development Finance Corp plans to increase direct equity investments, including in Africa and the critical minerals sector, the agency’s Africa head said, as the U.S. steps up efforts to counter China’s dominance of key supply chains.

Critical minerals have become a focal point of global competition, with the U.S. and other major economies seeking to secure supply chains for electric vehicles and renewable energy, while reducing dependence on China.

The DFC, the U.S. government’s main investment arm, said in September it would invest up to $155 million in African digital infrastructure provider WIOCC , its largest ever equity commitment.

DFC Regional Managing Director for Africa Vibhuti Jain told Reuters that, where strategically significant, “you will see us deploy equity in addition to or in place of other instruments”.

“There are a number of projects in our equity pipeline right now, including in Africa, (and) including in the critical minerals sector,” said Jain, without providing details.

She said the DFC would continue to provide more debt financing, credit guarantees and political risk insurance than equity investments for the foreseeable future.

“But I think as the agency continues to grow, we will do more equity investments,” she added.

Attention on Critical Minerals Sector

Jain said the DFC has more than $14 billion of investment commitments across Africa and that critical minerals projects, or projects linked to the sector, are a major driver of new investments.

The DFC said more than $3 billion of those commitments are in critical minerals.

“So really, this is a sector to which we’re paying close attention,” Jain said.

In addition to financing a pipeline of African critical minerals projects, including rare earths developments and a graphite mine in Mozambique, the DFC is backing the rehabilitation of the Lobito minerals transport corridor linking African copper and cobalt mines to the Atlantic coast.

items.title: New-look Maple Leafs face tough road test against Avalanche
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: After overhauling their roster over the offseason, grabbing five points in the first five games is not a bad start for the new-look Toronto Maple Leafs.
items.body:
After overhauling their roster over the offseason, grabbing five points in the first five games is not a bad start for the new-look Toronto Maple Leafs.
They go for two more when they visit the Colorado Avalanche on Saturday night in the midpoint of a three-game road trip that started in Las Vegas on Thursday night.
Toronto brought in eight new forwards, a new goaltender and a new head coach, looking to turn a last-place Atlantic Division finish in 2025-26 into a contending season. Jim Hiller, who was hired June 17 to lead the retooling, has experimented with different line combinations during games, trying to find the right mix of players.
"Just try to change the vibe a little bit at different times," Hiller explained after Thursday night's 4-3 shootout loss to the Golden Knights. "Some players have been pretty consistent night after night. But as for three at the same time, we're still looking for that."
The Maple Leafs made another move ahead of Saturday night's game when they brought up veteran forward Miles Wood from the AHL on Friday. Wood played two seasons with Colorado before being dealt to Columbus after the 2024-25 season.
Toronto acquired Wood from the Blue Jackets before this season, and he should make his Maple Leafs debut against his former team.
The new foundation for the organization starts with Gavin McKenna, the 18-year-old left winger who was the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 draft. McKenna has played in every game so far and scored his first NHL goal in a 5-4 overtime win against Nashville on Tuesday night.
McKenna will face arguably the toughest defensive corps in the NHL on Saturday night, headed by the top pairing of Cale Makar and Devon Toews. Colorado also boasts one of the top overall players in the league in Nathan MacKinnon, who has followed up his Rocket Richard Trophy-winning season with a hot start.
MacKinnon has three goals and five assists already this year, including a goal and two assists in Thursday's 7-3 win at Calgary. The victory came one night after losing at Winnipeg on a last-minute goal.
"Mentally, it's a grind to play back-to-backs and I think we have a really good head on our shoulders as a team of where we are and what we need to do in order to have success on the second night," Toews said.
Colorado made significant changes to its roster, and one of the moves is working out well early this season. The Avalanche brought in veteran forward Jaden Schwartz, who had two goals Thursday night and three on the season.
"He's been really good for us," Colorado coach Jared Bednar said of Schwartz. "A veteran guy. He's an incredible team guy. He does a little bit of everything for you. He's like a Swiss Army knife."
The Avalanche could be without Logan O'Connor on Saturday night. O'Connor, who has not yet played this season due to a lower-body injury, is away from the team due to the sudden passing of his father, NHL veteran Myles O'Connor.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Ella Langley show canceled over security threat; police say area is safe
items.author: Lisa Richwine
items.creator: Lisa Richwine
items.summary: Country music star Ella Langley's Friday night performance in Oklahoma was canceled shortly before it was scheduled to start over what the singer called a "serious security threat."
items.body:
Country music star Ella Langley's Friday night performance in Oklahoma was canceled shortly before it was scheduled to start over what the singer called a "serious security threat."
Police said they conducted security checks after a caller warned of harm but found no credible threat.
Langley, the singer of hit song "Choosin' Texas," had been scheduled to play at the 19,000-seat Bank of Oklahoma Center in Tulsa. About two hours before the planned start time, she and the venue alerted fans via social media that the show was called off.
"Due to a serious security threat involving the safety of my fans, the venue staff, and my team, the incredibly difficult decision was made to cancel tonight’s show," Langley said in a Facebook post. "This decision was made under the advisement of local authorities, the venue, and my security team."
A statement from the venue, known as the BOK Center, said that "after careful consideration, we have determined the show cannot proceed."
Tulsa Police Captain Richard Meulenberg, in a video posted on Facebook, said his department did not advise canceling the event. The show was cleared to go forward after a standard security sweep with bomb-sniffing dogs, he said. After that, a person called "saying that someone was going to do great harm" at the event with "shots fired and bombs."
Police conducted a second security sweep, Meulenberg said, and "advised the group that was supposed to be performing tonight that we could not find a credible threat."
"Everything is safe," he added.
Langley, 27, is a rising star in country music. "Choosin' Texas" made history last month after spending 23 weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart, breaking Mariah Carey's longstanding record of 22 weeks.
"I know how much time, travel, money, and planning goes into coming to a show, and I can’t tell you how sorry I am," Langley said in her statement. "This is not a decision that was made lightly. I was so looking forward to spending tonight with you, but your safety will always mean more to me than anything else. I refuse to put anyone in harm’s way."

items.title: Wall Street ve una señal preocupante en la caída del mercado de bonos de EE.UU.
items.author: Greg Ritchie
items.summary: La prima de plazo constituye, en esencia, una protección frente a giros impredecibles, desde crisis geopolíticas hasta crisis fiscales gubernamentales, que podrían afectar al mercado antes de que venz ...
items.body: Bloomberg — Es una de las señales menos comprendidas del mercado de renta fija, pero últimamente todos en Wall Street debaten qué significa su renovada presencia en el mercado. Se conoce como prima por plazo, o el pago adicional que los inversores exigen a cambio de los riesgos que implica poseer bonos del Tesoro a 10 años en lugar de simplemente renovar valores a corto plazo durante el mismo período. La forma exacta de medirla varía, al igual que las explicaciones de sus fluctuaciones. Ver más: ¿Conviene hoy una cartera con 60% de acciones y 40% de bonos? Esto dice Goldman Sachs Lo que no cabe duda es que, durante las últimas semanas, se disparó a niveles no vistos en más de una década e impulsó la última oleada de venta masiva de bonos, que ha llevado los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro estadounidense a su nivel más alto en 24 años. Esto, a su vez, aviva los temores de un posible cambio que ejercerá una mayor presión sobre un mercado ya maltrecho y mantendrá elevados los costos de endeudamiento en toda la economía. Esa prima de plazo constituye, en esencia, una protección frente a giros impredecibles, desde crisis geopolíticas hasta crisis fiscales gubernamentales, que podrían afectar al mercado antes de que venzan los bonos a largo plazo. Es distinto de las perspectivas actuales de inflación y de la dirección de la política monetaria, factores que también se reflejan en los rendimientos. Dado que la prima no es directamente observable y debe inferirse, Neel Kashkari, presidente del Banco de la Reserva Federal de Minneapolis, la comparó en una ocasión con la materia oscura, esa sustancia invisible que, según los físicos, explica algunos misterios cósmicos. “Hay varias maneras de calcularlo, pero todas apuntan a una tendencia alcista”, dijo Frank Rybinski, jefe de estrategia macroeconómica de Aegon Asset Management. “Y eso me indica que este movimiento tiene potencial para mantenerse”. Ver más: ¿Dónde invertir en bonos de América Latina? Las oportunidades que ve Goldman Sachs “La fuerte revalorización de la prima por plazo implícita en los bonos del Tesoro —con la prima a 10 años alcanzando su nivel más alto en 12 años— sugiere que los inversores exigen una mayor compensación por mantener la inversión a largo plazo en medio de la creciente incertidumbre fiscal y geopolítica”. — Frank Monkam, estratega de mercados macroeconómicos. No hubo un catalizador claro. Los analistas de Barclays, liderados por Demi Hu, señalaron que la incertidumbre macroeconómica, la ruptura de las correlaciones habituales entre los movimientos de las acciones y los bonos, el aumento de la oferta de deuda y las preocupaciones sobre la política fiscal son factores que influyen en la prima de plazo y podrían estar desempeñando un papel importante. Neil Shearing, economista jefe del grupo Capital Economics, señaló que el reciente movimiento podría reflejar factores técnicos, como los ajustes de cartera a finales del mes pasado, o los efectos secundarios de la creciente preocupación en Europa por la carga de la deuda francesa. Stephen Douglass, economista jefe de NISA Investment Advisors, señaló algunos indicios de tensión en los mercados de crédito, así como dudas más generalizadas entre los inversores sobre las ventajas de mantener activos de renta fija en un contexto en el que las perturbaciones inflacionistas son cada vez más frecuentes. “No es una historia sencilla”, dijo Douglass, quien advirtió que no hay que sobreinterpretar las fluctuaciones a corto plazo. “Pero diría que creo que nos encontramos en un entorno de primas de seguros a plazo en alza”. Esto supone un motivo de preocupación para los partidarios de los bonos. Una prima de plazo estructuralmente más elevada podría mantener altas las tasas de interés a largo plazo, impidiendo que el mercado se recupere de su caída. Este indicador descendió de forma constante en la década de 1990, cuando la creciente globalización ejercía una fuerza deflacionaria, y cayó aún más durante la década de 2010, a medida que los programas de flexibilización cuantitativa de los bancos centrales distorsionaban los mercados mundiales de bonos al inundarlos de liquidez. Llegó a situarse en un mínimo del -1,7% en marzo de 2020, cuando los inversores buscaban refugio en los bonos, antes de repuntar de forma sostenida hasta alcanzar valores positivos a partir de finales de 2024, según un modelo elaborado por economistas de la Reserva Federal de Nueva York. Ver más: Veterano de Morgan Stanley se vuelve optimista con bonos de EE.UU. por primera vez en una década Se había mantenido relativamente estable durante la mayor parte de la ola de ventas que se inició tras el inicio de la guerra de EE.UU. contra Irán a finales de febrero. A mediados de septiembre, comenzó a dispararse. El modelo de la Reserva Federal de Nueva York muestra que subió alrededor de 40 puntos básicos, hasta aproximadamente el 0,98%, el nivel más alto desde 2014 y más que suficiente para explicar el aumento de casi 30 puntos básicos en los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro a 10 años durante ese período. La estimación de Bloomberg Economics muestra un incremento similar. Otra estimación, que incorpora las previsiones de los economistas sobre la política de la Reserva Federal en el cálculo, ha subido hasta el 1,08%, el nivel más alto desde 2010. Ese repunte se produjo cuando otros factores que influyen en los precios apenas variaron. Las expectativas de inflación se han mantenido estables. La decisión unánime de la Reserva Federal de subir los tipos de interés el mes pasado disipó algunas preocupaciones sobre su compromiso de controlar los precios al consumidor. Y el petróleo, aunque se encuentra por encima de los US$100 el barril, se ha mantenido en un rango estrecho. Un aumento sostenido de la prima de plazo se sumaría a la presión que ejercen sobre el mercado la elevada inflación, el sólido crecimiento económico y la avalancha de préstamos solicitados por empresas que invierten en inteligencia artificial y por gobiernos de todo el mundo con déficit. La presidenta del Banco de la Reserva Federal de Dallas, Lorie Logan, afirmó la semana pasada que una prima de plazo al alza, al elevar los costos de financiación, podría ralentizar la economía y reducir la necesidad de que el banco central aumente las tasas de interés. Ver más: Bonos del Tesoro de EE.UU. retoman caída y rendimiento a 30 años alcanza máximo desde 2002 “El mercado de bonos ya no espera a que la Reserva Federal endurezca las condiciones financieras”, afirmó Florian Ielpo, jefe de macroeconomía de Lombard Odier Investment Managers. “Las elevadas primas a largo plazo, la incertidumbre inflacionaria y las necesidades de endeudamiento público pueden mantener los rendimientos a largo plazo en niveles restrictivos, incluso cuando la trayectoria prevista de las tasas a corto plazo se vuelve menos agresiva”. Una de las razones que explican los últimos movimientos podría ser el efecto de contagio de la venta masiva y desordenada de bonos franceses. Algunos también señalan la actividad de cobertura por parte de los titulares de valores respaldados por hipotecas, que puede exagerar temporalmente los movimientos del mercado. Sin embargo, tras todo esto podrían acechar riesgos a largo plazo que se han ido acumulando en la economía global. Uno de ellos es que las perturbaciones en el suministro de energía y otras materias primas —como las que siguieron a la invasión rusa de Ucrania y la guerra de Estados Unidos contra Irán— podrían volverse más frecuentes a medida que se acentúan las divisiones geopolíticas. Luego está el déficit presupuestario del gobierno federal de US$2 billones, equivalente a aproximadamente el 6% del producto interno bruto del país, un nivel de estímulo históricamente alto en un momento de bajo desempleo y sólido crecimiento económico. Si bien la administración Trump ha prometido repetidamente controlar el gasto, hay pocas expectativas de que eso suceda pronto. “El panorama macroeconómico está plagado de riesgos, lo que debería traducirse en una prima de riesgo a plazo saludable”, afirmó Mark Malek, director de inversiones de Siebert Financial. “Cada vez que surge una noticia impactante, los inversores recuerdan ese riesgo”. --Con la colaboración de Christopher Anstey. items.title: ＮＢＡ＝レブロン、シクサーズでのプレシーズン初戦で10得点
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［９日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［９日　ロイター］ - 米プロバスケットボール協会（ＮＢＡ）のセブンティシクサーズに加入したレブロン・ジェームズ（４１）は８日、ネッツとのプレシーズン戦で移籍後初出場を果たし、１０得点５アシストを記録した。

レブロンはフィールドゴールの試投がわずか１本だったものの、フリースロー８本を全て成功させた。プレーしたのは前半のみで後半は出場せず、シクサーズは１０８─１１４で敗れた。

レブロンは試合後、「新しいユニホームを着ていたのは確かだが、バスケットボールはバスケットボール。コート上でプレーするものだ」と語り、これまで練習でともに汗を流してきたチームメートと実戦に臨めたことを喜んだ。

レブロンは７月、フリーエージェント（ＦＡ）として２年総額８００万ドル（約１２億７０００万円）、選手オプション付きの契約で加入。昨季はレーカーズで６０試合に出場し、１試合平均２０．９得点６．１リバウンド７．２アシストを記録した。

オールスター選出２２回を誇るレブロンは、通算出場試合数（１６２２）と通算得点（４万３４４０）でＮＢＡ歴代最多記録を保持。ヒートで２回、キャバリアーズとレーカーズで各１回、ＮＢＡ制覇を果たしている。

items.title: Libya's military seizes narcotics after firefight with smugglers
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Libya's military brigade seized more than 1.3 million narcotic pills after a firefight with smugglers in a southeastern town that injured three soldiers, the military said on Friday.
items.body:
Libya's military brigade seized more than 1.3 million narcotic pills after a firefight with smugglers in a southeastern town that injured three soldiers, the military said on Friday.
The north African nation has become a major regional transit hub for synthetic drugs and other narcotics en route to domestic users and elsewhere in the continent, the UN said in January.
In a statement, a military media unit said the Subul al-Salam infantry brigade in Kufra, about 1,700 km (1,000 miles) from the capital, Tripoli, targeted hideouts used by traffickers of narcotics and illicit goods.
Pictures it posted showed soldiers standing around tens of transparent plastic small bags filled with round white pills bearing the number one and a sentence in black that read "made in Germany".
The brigade operates under the Land Forces General Staff and owes responsibility to the military commander Khalifa Haftar of the eastern-based Libyan National Army.
The statement gave no value for the drugs seized.
Drug gangs have exploited the tumultuous situation in the country since 2011, the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime said in a January report.
Libya plunged into a prolonged period of internal conflict and division after former ruler Muammar Gaddafi was toppled in a NATO-backed uprising that year.
Five people were handed death sentences by a court in the Western Mountains region, about 160 km (100 miles) southwest of Tripoli, for importing more than 2 million pills of psychotropic substances, the attorney general said in October.
(This story has been refiled to change the word 'responsible' to 'responsibilty,' in paragraph 5.)

前日１７位の米沢は４バーディー、２ボギーの６９で回り、通算５アンダーの１３７。１２位スタートの松山英樹は３バーディー、４ボギーの７２とスコアを落とし、通算３アンダーの３０位に後退した。

同じく１２位で出た久常涼は７１で回り、通算４アンダーの１３８で２６位。金谷拓実と砂川公佑は３０位、岩田寛と石坂友宏は３８位、藤本佳則と細野勇策は４６位、香妻陣一朗は５４位、中島啓太は６１位、岩崎亜久竜は６３位、アマチュアの長崎煌心は７０位だった。

首位には通算１１アンダーでキース・ミッチェルとジェーコブ・ブリッジマン（ともに米国）が並んだ。ミッチェルは８バーディー、２ボギーの６５で６つ伸ばし、ブリッジマンは４バーディー、１ボギーの６８で回った。

items.title: Presidenta encargada de Venezuela autoriza operaciones de Starlink en el país
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: La presidenta encargada de Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez, ha autorizado a Starlink —el servicio de internet por satélite operado por SpaceX, empresa de Elon Musk— a operar en el país sudamericano.
items.body:
La presidenta encargada de Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez, ha autorizado a Starlink —el servicio de internet por satélite operado por SpaceX, empresa de Elon Musk— a operar en el país sudamericano.
La autorización forma parte de un acuerdo con la firma estadounidense, según informó el gobierno venezolano en un comunicado el viernes.
"Con esta medida, se autoriza legalmente la prestación del servicio de internet satelital de la marca Starlink en todo el territorio nacional, lo que permitirá una operación formal con domicilio y fiscalización en el país. Con este otorgamiento, el Estado venezolano ratifica su compromiso con el ordenamiento del espectro radioeléctrico, el fomento de las nuevas tecnologías", agregó el gobierno en comunicado.
La división de internet por satélite de la empresa ha seguido ampliando su base global de suscriptores, impulsada por el lanzamiento de satélites adicionales y una gama creciente de servicios para consumidores, empresas, el sector de la aviación, el ámbito marítimo y el gobierno

items.title: US-Ukraine-European negotiators meet in Miami as Trump announces diesel deal with Russia
items.author: Steve Holland
items.creator: Steve Holland
items.summary: Negotiators held six hours of talks to reach an agreement on a proposal to end the war in Ukraine.
items.body:
Negotiators for the US, Ukraine and Europeans held six hours of talks in Miami on Friday with the aim of reaching agreement on a unified proposal to end the war in Ukraine, a person familiar with the talks said.
The goal is to reach agreement on such a proposal in the coming weeks so it can be presented to Russia in order to seek a breakthrough before the winter, said the person, who spoke on condition of anonymity.
The talks came on the same day that US President Donald Trump said Russia had agreed to [USN:S0N43U024 TEXT:"supply diesel to global markets"] in an effort to lower fuel prices, while his administration lifted sanctions on Russian fuel that were designed to deprive Moscow of revenues for the war. The deal was criticized by US lawmakers and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy.
"All that money goes toward the war against people, against Ukraine, against all of us. I believe our team is simply being used as a smokescreen. And that is certainly not fair," Zelenskiy said in a statement.
Russian President Vladimir Putin said after a call with Trump that an immediate [USN:L1N45V0ZL TEXT:"resumption of peace talks was unlikely"], citing Ukrainian drone attacks on Moscow.
The talks in Miami included US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and delegations from Ukraine as well as representatives from Europe and NATO.
The negotiators covered a lengthy list of topics in the discussions, including a post-war package for Ukraine that would include security guarantees from the US and from Europe, the person said.
Also discussed were a post-war economic plan for Ukraine and a pathway to accession to the European Union for Kyiv, the person said.
In a sensitive subject, the delegations discussed "some ideas" on territory, the person said, declining to elaborate.
Ukraine has been adamant that Russia cede territory it has seized during the conflict. President Donald Trump has said both sides will need to compromise.
The person said the delegations also discussed a Europe-Russia security architecture that would set the stage for peaceful years ahead. The person did not provide details.
