items.title: Trump leva à Suprema Corte dos EUA ação contra Hillary Clinton relativa à eleição de 2016
items.author: Andrew Chung
items.creator: Andrew Chung
items.summary: O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, solicitou nesta sexta-feira à Suprema Corte que restabelecesse sua ação judicial indeferida contra sua rival democrata nas eleições de 2016, Hillary Clinton, na qual a acusava de conspirar com o ex-diretor do FBI James Comey e outros para manipular a eleição daquele ano, associando sua campanha à Rússia.
items.body:
O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, solicitou nesta sexta-feira à Suprema Corte que restabelecesse sua ação judicial indeferida contra sua rival democrata nas eleições de 2016, Hillary Clinton, na qual a acusava de conspirar com o ex-diretor do FBI James Comey e outros para manipular a eleição daquele ano, associando sua campanha à Rússia.
O presidente republicano entrou com o recurso depois que um juiz federal indeferiu o processo e impôs quase US$1 milhão em sanções contra Trump e uma de suas advogadas por terem movido uma ação “frívola”. Posteriormente, um tribunal de apelação dos EUA manteve o indeferimento e as sanções.
Em 2022, quando já não ocupava o cargo após perder a eleição de 2020, Trump processou Hillary, Comey, o ex-oficial da inteligência britânica Christopher Steele, o Comitê Nacional Democrata e vários outros em uma longa ação movida no tribunal federal da Flórida.
Trump, que tem um histórico de processar adversários, alegou que, na corrida para a eleição de 2016, Hillary conspirou com aliados para desacreditá-lo por meio de uma “narrativa falsa” de que ele e sua campanha teriam agido em conluio com a Rússia. A longa ação alegava “criminalidade organizada” e uma “conspiração para cometer falsidade prejudicial”, entre outras alegações.
Trump derrotou Hillary naquela eleição, apesar de ter perdido o voto popular nacional, e cumpriu seu primeiro mandato de 2017 a 2021.
Autoridades do governo dos EUA acusaram a Rússia de interferir na eleição de 2016, e uma investigação liderada pelo ex-chefe do FBI Robert Mueller documentou contatos extensos entre a campanha de Trump e agentes russos que buscavam influenciar a eleição a seu favor. Trump chamou a ideia de interferência russa de “farsa”.
Desde que perdeu para o democrata Joe Biden em 2020, Trump tem feito alegações falsas de fraude eleitoral generalizada na eleição daquele ano. Trump reconquistou a Presidência ao derrotar a democrata Kamala Harris em 2024 e continua a fazer essas alegações falsas.
O juiz federal Donald Middlebrooks indeferiu a ação movida por Trump contra Clinton, citando inúmeras falhas, incluindo o fato de Trump ter esperado tempo demais para apresentar algumas das alegações. O juiz comparou a ação de Trump a um “manifesto político de duzentas páginas que expõe suas queixas contra aqueles que se opuseram a ele”.
Middlebrooks posteriormente ordenou que Trump e sua principal advogada no caso, Alina Habba, pagassem quase US$1 milhão em honorários e custas, impondo as sanções por terem movido uma ação que, segundo o juiz, tinha como objetivo “promover de forma desonesta uma narrativa política”. O juiz também repreendeu Trump e seus advogados por um “padrão contínuo de uso indevido dos tribunais”.
Middlebrooks concluiu que a ação utilizou táticas processuais abusivas, continha alegações factuais “conscientemente falsas” e invocava teorias jurídicas “frívolas”.
O Tribunal Federal de Apelações do 11º Circuito, com sede em Atlanta, manteve as decisões do juiz em 2025, incluindo as sanções.

items.body:
Venezuela's interim President Delcy Rodriguez has authorized Starlink, the satellite internet service operated by Elon Musk's SpaceX (SPCX.O) , to operate in the Latin American country.
The authorization is part of an agreement with the US firm, the Venezuelan government said in a statement on Friday.
The company's satellite-internet unit has continued to expand its global subscriber base, aided by launches of additional satellites and a growing range of consumer, enterprise, aviation, maritime and government services.

items.title: David Puig leaves LIV as Bryson DeChambeau reportedly eyes Europe starts
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The DP World Tour, formerly known as the European Tour, may hold the key for many players departing LIV Golf.
items.body:
The DP World Tour, formerly known as the European Tour, may hold the key for many players departing LIV Golf.
Spanish youngster David Puig announced Thursday that he would not stay with LIV as it restructures for the future, switching his membership to the DP World Tour. And two-time major champion Bryson DeChambeau is reportedly weighing more starts in Europe, as well.
"I don't see myself playing in the LIV 2.0," Puig told reporters at the Spanish Open, a DP World Tour event. "It's a decision I've made. I hope to play the European Tour next year, which I really enjoy, with a fuller schedule."
Puig, 24, was a strong amateur golfer and starred collegiately at Arizona State. He played in two LIV events while still an amateur in 2022, when the league was still in its infancy, and signed with LIV once he turned pro.
While Puig never won an individual tournament title in his four-plus years with LIV, he maintained eligibility for some DP World Tour and Asian Tour events and earned the biggest win of his career last November at the Australian PGA Championship.
In pursuing full-time DP World Tour membership, Puig follows Spanish stars Jon Rahm and Sergio Garcia from LIV back to Europe. Puig played for Garcia's Fireballs GC while with the team-based league. Garcia was granted release from his LIV contract earlier this week.
DeChambeau and Rahm, meanwhile, are among the small number of elite players whose decisions will make or break the so-called LIV 2.0 plan. Rahm made his decision known earlier this week that he would leave LIV, and golf insider Alan Shipnuck reported late last month that DeChambeau was still going back and forth on his final decision.
The Telegraph reported that DeChambeau's team has contacted DP World Tour brass about which tournaments he could appear at in 2027.
The report made clear that DeChambeau is not pursuing membership on the European tour, the way Patrick Reed did when he left LIV at the start of 2026, a path Rahm will now emulate.
LIV members have until Oct. 25 to commit to playing for the league next year. LIV still needs commitments from a sufficient number of players with outstanding financial claims against the league to satisfy the terms set by its restructuring partner, BC Partners Credit.
--Field Level Media

items.title: UAW President Shawn Fain declares victory in race for second term
items.author: Kalea Hall
items.creator: Kalea Hall
items.summary: United Auto Workers President Shawn Fain declared victory on Friday in a race to maintain his position as head of the 400,000-member union.
items.body:
United Auto Workers President Shawn Fain declared victory on Friday in a race to maintain his position as head of the 400,000-member union.
Fain, 57, who rose to national prominence during a 2023 strike against General Motors (GM.N) , Ford (F.N) and Chrysler-parent Stellantis (STLAM.MI) , received a majority of the votes and easily topped five challengers, according to preliminary ballot totals released by a federal monitor overseeing the vote.
Fain had widely been expected to win the balloting, which the Detroit Three automakers were watching closely as they look ahead to 2028 contract negotiations. The companies are wary of raising their labor costs at a time when the auto industry is grappling with weaker vehicle demand and intensifying competition.
“One thing I know about our membership is they're ready to fight,” Fain said in an interview with Reuters. “They know they deserve better. And let's not fool ourselves. All these companies are massively profitable.”
Fain has pointed to the next round of negotiations as an opportunity to secure gains beyond the union's landmark 2023 contract, which delivered wage increases of more than 25% over the four-year life of the agreement. The UAW is already urging members to strike in the spring of 2028, when current contracts with the Detroit automakers expire.
GM, Ford and Stellantis did not immediately respond to requests for comment on Fain's declared victory late Friday.
FAIN’S COMBATIVE APPROACH LED TO GAINS In 2023, just months after narrowly winning his seat, Fain took an unorthodox, combative stance against the automakers.
He insisted on bargaining with all three automakers at once, a departure from past practice, in which the union got an agreement at one company to use as a template for the other two. Eventually, he launched simultaneous strikes at factories across all three automakers, a first for the union.
“Shawn Fain will continue to take an aggressive approach to collective bargaining. The challenge this time will be that the companies will be well aware” of that approach, said Stephen Silvia, a labor expert from American University.
DETROIT AUTOMAKERS LEERY OF LABOR-COST INCREASES Fain said on Friday that in 2028 he plans to push to restore pensions for all workers, a benefit that ended for new hires in 2007, around the time of the near-collapse of domestic US auto companies.
GM, Ford and Stellantis, meanwhile, have been stung by tariff expenses, higher raw-materials costs and an expensive rollback of their electric-vehicle plans amid weak US demand. Executives are likely to push back against any meaningful labor-cost increases, said Marick Masters, business professor emeritus at Detroit’s Wayne State University.
“The recipe is there for a major confrontation with the companies being in a less favorable position to withstand the pressures,” he said.

items.title: テニス＝マスターズ上海大会、坂本が3回戦進出　ジョコビッチは敗退
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［上海　９日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［上海　９日　ロイター］ - テニスのマスターズ上海大会は９日、男子シングルス２回戦を行い、予選勝者の坂本怜が第２３シードでロシア出身のアンドレイ・ルブレフを６─４、６─４のストレートで破り、３回戦進出を果たした。

世界ランキング１３７位の坂本は第１セットの第１ゲームでブレークに成功。第２セットも第９ゲームで相手のサービスゲームを破り、元世界５位の格上選手から金星を挙げた。３回戦では第９シードのアレックス・デミノー（オーストラリア）と対戦する。

過去４回優勝の第１０シード、ノバク・ジョコビッチ（セルビア）はフベルト・フルカチュ（ポーランド）に４─６、３─６で敗れ、初戦で姿を消した。

ジョコビッチはこれまでフルカチュとの対戦で８戦全勝だった。試合後、「北京でプレーしていた時の状態には程遠かった。少し疲れていて、フレッシュではなかった」と振り返った。

第１シードのアレクサンダー・ズベレフ（ドイツ）、第３シードのベン・シェルトン（米国）は順当に勝利した。

前半に清家貴子が先制点を挙げた日本は、浜野まいか、長谷川唯のゴールで加点。１点を返されて３─１とリードして迎えた後半には、途中出場の千葉玲海菜、土方麻椰もネットを揺らした。

日本はこの後、１３日にドイツのブレーメンでドイツと対戦する。

items.title: Ukraine-Poutine minimise une reprise immédiate des discussions, dit le Kremlin
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Le président russe Vladimir Poutine a dit vendredi à son homologue américain Donald Trump que Kyiv avait sapé la possibilité d'une reprise immédiate des négociations de paix trilatérales après avoir mené des frappes de drones à Moscou durant les élections législatives qui se sont déroulées le mois dernier, a fait savoir le Kremlin.
items.body:
Le président russe Vladimir Poutine a dit vendredi à son homologue américain Donald Trump que Kyiv avait sapé la possibilité d'une reprise immédiate des négociations de paix trilatérales après avoir mené des frappes de drones à Moscou durant les élections législatives qui se sont déroulées le mois dernier, a fait savoir le Kremlin.
Vladimir Poutine avait dit que Moscou était prêt à reprendre les négociations avec Kyiv après la tenue des élections législatives. L'Ukraine a toutefois lancé des attaques contre la capitale russe et a frappé des bureaux de vote, ce qui, selon le chef du Kremlin, a mis en péril le processus de paix.
"En lançant le jour le plus important des élections une attaque de drones à grande échelle contre Moscou, d'autres villes et des bureaux de votes, et en prenant pour cible certaines personnes impliquées dans l'organisation des élections, le régime de Kyiv a, en réalité, interrompu la possibilité d'une reprise immédiate du processus de négociation", a déclaré le conseiller du Kremlin Iouri Ouchakov.
"Comme le président l'a dit, nous allons désormais évaluer quand ces négociations pourront reprendre", a-t-il ajouté au sujet des discussions trilatérales entre la Russie, les Etats-Unis et l'Ukraine.
Iouri Ouchakov a indiqué que, durant leur appel, Vladimir Poutine et Donald Trump avaient abordé d'importantes initiatives économiques, notamment de potentielles livraisons de carburant russe.
Donald Trump a annoncé vendredi qu'à l'issue d'une discussion "très fructueuse" qu'il avait eue avec Vladimir Poutine, la Russie avait accepté de livrer immédiatement plus de 300.000 tonnes de [USN:L8N45V1O6 TEXT:"diesel"] sur les marchés américain et mondial.

items.title: Alcolumbre pauta para 4ª-feira votação da PEC do fim da jornada 6x1
items.author: Maria Marcello
items.creator: Maria Marcello
items.summary: O presidente do Senado, Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP), pautou a votação da Proposta de Emenda à Constituição (PEC) que extingue a jornada de trabalho conhecida como 6x1 e reduz a jornada de trabalho semanal para a próxima quarta-feira, quando ocorre a quinta sessão de discussão da matéria.
items.body:
O presidente do Senado, Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP), pautou a votação da Proposta de Emenda à Constituição (PEC) que extingue a jornada de trabalho conhecida como 6x1 e reduz a jornada de trabalho semanal para a próxima quarta-feira, quando ocorre a quinta sessão de discussão da matéria.
Pelas regras regimentais, qualquer PEC precisa passar por cinco sessões de discussão para então ser votada em primeiro turno -- o Senado já realizou três dessas sessões nesta semana, e tem mais duas previstas para a próxima, na terça e na quarta-feira.
"Pautei para quarta-feira (14) a votação, em primeiro turno, da PEC 221, de 2019, que trata do fim da escala 6x1", disse o presidente do Senado em nota distribuída por sua assessoria.
"Cumpro, assim, o compromisso de colocar a proposta em votação, com responsabilidade, diálogo e respeito ao rito regimental. Caberá a cada senador e a cada senadora decidir com liberdade, consciência e convicção", acrescentou o senador.
O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, que concorre à reeleição, é favorável à PEC e tem usado a defesa de sua aprovação como plataforma de campanha. Lula chegou a desafiar o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) -- que venceu o primeiro turno da disputa presidencial no domingo e enfrenta Lula no dia 25 de outubro --, e seu partido a votarem favoravelmente à proposta.
Flávio, que se opõe à PEC, acusa Lula de estar sendo oportunista. O senador e seus aliados têm defendido em declarações públicas uma proposta alternativa que leve em conta uma jornada flexível e a remuneração proporcional à hora trabalhada, defendendo a prevalência de acordos individuais entre empregados e patrões sobre convenções coletivas.
Caso seja aprovada em primeiro turno, com no mínimo 49 votos, a PEC precisa ser discutida por mais três sessões, para então ser votada em segundo turno.
Segundo a Agência Senado, a líder do governo no Senado, senadora Teresa Leitão (PT-PE), está coletando assinaturas para um requerimento que possa acelerar o calendário de votação da PEC, de forma a ter sua tramitação concluída na Casa na penúltima semana de outubro, antes do segundo turno da eleição presidencial.
A PEC em discussão no Senado prevê que a jornada de trabalho terá uma redução de 2 horas semanais das 44 atuais já nos 60 dias depois que a proposta for promulgada. A carga horária sofrerá um decréscimo de mais 2 horas um ano após a primeira redução.
A proposta também estabelece o piso de duas folgas semanais, uma delas preferencialmente no domingo, e garante que não haverá redução de salário.

items.title: Trump takes suit against Hillary Clinton over 2016 election to Supreme Court
items.author: Andrew Chung
items.creator: Andrew Chung
items.summary: President Donald Trump asked the US Supreme Court on Friday to revive his dismissed lawsuit against his 2016 Democratic rival Hillary Clinton accusing her of conspiring along with former FBI Director James Comey and others to rig that year's election by linking his campaign to Russia.
items.body:
President Donald Trump asked the US Supreme Court on Friday to revive his dismissed lawsuit against his 2016 Democratic rival Hillary Clinton accusing her of conspiring along with former FBI Director James Comey and others to rig that year's election by linking his campaign to Russia.
The Republican president filed his appeal after a federal judge threw out the case and imposed nearly $1 million in sanctions against Trump and one of his lawyers for bringing a "frivolous" suit. A US appeals court subsequently upheld the dismissal and sanctions.
Trump's lawyers wrote in the appeal that Supreme Court review of the case is needed in order to protect the presidency. They wrote that the decisions by the lower courts reflect "a deeply troubling trend of federal courts using sanctions and disciplinary threats to punish the president and his lawyers for legitimate legal positions that those courts (erroneously) reject."
In 2022, when he was out of office after losing the 2020 election, Trump sued Clinton, Comey, former British intelligence officer Christopher Steele, the Democratic National Committee and numerous others in a lengthy complaint filed in federal court in Florida.
Trump, who has a history of suing adversaries, alleged that in the lead-up to the 2016 election, Clinton conspired with allies to discredit him with a "false narrative" that he and his campaign colluded with Russia. The lengthy suit alleged "racketeering" and a "conspiracy to commit injurious falsehood," among other claims.
Trump defeated Clinton in that election, despite losing the national popular vote, and served his first term in office from 2017 to 2021.
US government officials have accused Russia of meddling in the 2016 election, and an investigation led by former FBI chief Robert Mueller documented extensive contacts between members of the Trump campaign and Russian operatives who sought to influence the election in his favor. Trump has called the idea of Russian interference a "hoax."
Since losing to Democrat Joe Biden in 2020, Trump has made false claims of widespread voting fraud in that year's election. Trump regained the presidency by defeating Democrat Kamala Harris in 2024, and has continued to make those false claims.
'POLITICAL MANIFESTO' US District Judge Donald Middlebrooks [USN:L1N30G0Q8 TEXT:"dismissed"] Trump's lawsuit against Clinton, citing numerous inadequacies, including that Trump waited too long to bring some of the claims. The judge likened Trump's lawsuit to a "two-hundred-page political manifesto outlining his grievances against those that have opposed him."
Middlebrooks later ordered Trump and his lead attorney in the case, Alina Habba, to pay nearly $1 million in fees and costs, imposing the [USN:L1N345068 TEXT:"sanctions"] for bringing a case that the judge said was intended "to dishonestly advance a political narrative." The judge also faulted Trump and his lawyers for a "continuing pattern of misuse of the courts."
Middlebrooks found that the lawsuit used abusive litigation tactics, contained "knowingly false" factual allegations and asserted "frivolous" legal theories.
The Atlanta-based 11th US Circuit Court of Appeals upheld the judge's rulings in 2025, including the sanctions.
"Many of Trump's and Habba's legal arguments were indeed frivolous," the 11th Circuit stated.
In Friday's filing, lawyers for Trump and Habba said the time limit for filing the lawsuit should have been extended because he chose to defer suing during his first term in office in order to carry out his constitutional responsibilities as president.
"This court's intervention is necessary to protect the presidency, and to prevent judicial disagreement from becoming a license to punish its advocates," the filing stated.
Mueller, serving as a special counsel appointed by the Justice Department, issued a [USN:KCN1RU2MF TEXT:"2019 report"] on his investigation. The report stated that Russia "interfered in the 2016 presidential election in sweeping and systematic fashion," but also stated that "the investigation did not establish that members of the Trump campaign conspired or coordinated with the Russian government in its election interference activities."
Mueller said in his report that he found "numerous links" and that the Trump campaign "expected it would benefit" from Russia's effort to tilt the election in Trump's favor.
Trump's then-Attorney General William Barr appointed a different special counsel, John Durham, in 2019 to look into potential missteps by the FBI.
In a [USN:L1N37C2MA TEXT:"2023 report"], Durham concluded that the FBI lacked "actual evidence" to investigate Trump's 2016 presidential campaign and relied too heavily on tips provided by Trump's political opponents to fuel the probe.
Trump's Justice Department last year indicted Comey, one of several adversaries of the president hit with criminal charges, accusing him of making false statements and obstructing Congress after he was accused of lying about authorizing leaks to the news media. A federal judge subsequently [USN:S0N3U5043 TEXT:"dismissed the indictment"], finding that the prosecutor who Trump handpicked to prosecute Comey had been unlawfully appointed.
Steele, working for an opposition research firm that was hired by a law firm on behalf of the Clinton campaign and the Democratic National Committee, produced a dossier that alleged ties between Trump's campaign and Russia as well as other salacious accusations, all of which Trump denied.

items.title: Em conversa telefônica com Trump, Putin minimizou chance de retomada imediata das negociações com Ucrânia, diz Kremlin
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: O presidente russo, Vladimir Putin, disse ao presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, nesta sexta-feira, que Kiev havia prejudicado a possibilidade de uma retomada imediata das negociações trilaterais de paz na Ucrânia depois de ter atacado Moscou com drones durante as eleições do mês passado, informou o Kremlin.
items.body:
O presidente russo, Vladimir Putin, disse ao presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, nesta sexta-feira, que Kiev havia prejudicado a possibilidade de uma retomada imediata das negociações trilaterais de paz na Ucrânia depois de ter atacado Moscou com drones durante as eleições do mês passado, informou o Kremlin.
Trump tem tentado, até o momento sem sucesso, intermediar um acordo de paz para pôr fim à guerra na Ucrânia, que teve início com a invasão russa em fevereiro de 2022.
O secretário de Estado dos EUA, Marco Rubio, afirmou na quinta-feira que a guerra da Rússia na Ucrânia está em um impasse perigoso e que os Estados Unidos continuarão trabalhando em busca de um acordo para pôr fim ao conflito.
Putin havia afirmado que Moscou estava pronta para retomar as negociações com Kiev após as eleições parlamentares russas do mês passado, mas a Ucrânia lançou ataques contra Moscou e atingiu seções eleitorais, colocando o processo de paz em risco, segundo ele.
“Ao lançar um ataque maciço com drones contra Moscou, outras cidades e seções eleitorais, bem como contra indivíduos específicos envolvidos na organização da eleição, no dia principal da votação, o regime de Kiev efetivamente inviabilizou a possibilidade de uma retomada imediata do processo de negociação”, disse o assessor de política externa do Kremlin, Yuri Ushakov, sobre a ligação com Trump.
“E agora, como disse o presidente, vamos avaliar quando essas negociações poderão ser retomadas”, acrescentou ele, referindo-se às negociações trilaterais envolvendo os EUA, a Rússia e a Ucrânia.
Ushakov também disse que Putin e Trump discutiram importantes iniciativas econômicas durante a ligação, incluindo possíveis fornecimentos de combustível russo.
Trump havia dito mais cedo, após a ligação com Putin, que a Rússia havia concordado em fornecer diesel imediatamente aos mercados dos EUA e globais, em um esforço para reduzir os preços dos combustíveis antes das eleições de meio de mandato nos EUA no mês que vem, embora analistas tenham afirmado que as quantidades provavelmente não reduziriam os preços de forma significativa.

items.title: Protesta en mina de cobre de Antofagasta en Chile se intensifica con huelga de hambre
items.author: James Attwood
items.summary: Las tensiones laborales en el sector minero se han intensificado este año, ya que los trabajadores reclaman una mayor participación en los beneficios extraordinarios derivados del alza de los precios.
items.body: Bloomberg — Los trabajadores de una mina de cobre de Antofagasta Plc en Chile intensificaron el viernes una huelga de tres días, con tres miembros del sindicato que iniciaron una huelga de hambre para presionar a la empresa a volver a la mesa de negociación. “No permita que sus trabajadores, hombres y mujeres, tengan que recurrir a medidas extremas como una huelga de hambre solo para que usted se siente a hablar”, dijo José Manuel Díaz, presidente de la principal federación laboral de Chile, a los periodistas en un campamento de protesta frente a las oficinas corporativas de Antofagasta en Santiago. Ver más: Servicio Militar 2027 en Chile: qué sanciones hay por no presentarse y cuándo se aplica una multa Las huelgas de hambre son una forma poco habitual de protesta en los conflictos laborales del sector minero chileno, aunque existen precedentes, como la acción de los líderes sindicales en las explotaciones de Codelco en 2020 y una huelga de hambre de 27 días en la mina Escondida del Grupo BHP en 2015. Las tensiones laborales en el sector minero se han intensificado este año, ya que los trabajadores reclaman una mayor participación en los beneficios extraordinarios derivados del alza de los precios. Las interrupciones en el suministro, las perturbaciones comerciales y la creciente demanda hicieron que el precio del cobre alcanzara el mes pasado un máximo histórico cercano a los US$15.000 por tonelada, y algunos analistas han pronosticado nuevas subidas. En una acción independiente, los supervisores de la mina de Escondida se encuentran en un proceso de mediación obligatoria con BHP para evitar una huelga que podría comenzar el martes. Díaz hizo un llamamiento directo a la multimillonaria familia Luksic de Chile, que controla Antofagasta. “No pedimos privilegios; solo pedimos un trato igualitario y, sobre todo, respeto”, afirmó. Unos 50 miembros del sindicato de Centinela han montado un campamento en el distrito financiero de Santiago, mientras que los trabajadores también se están manifestando frente a la mina, en el norte de Chile. Antofagasta se ha negado a hacer comentarios sobre la huelga de hambre. Ver más: ¿En qué invertir en Chile, Perú y Colombia? Estas son las apuestas de este banco de inversión Los sindicatos afirman que el principal punto de conflicto son las diferencias salariales y de beneficios entre empleados que desempeñan las mismas funciones pero pertenecen a distintos sindicatos. Los dirigentes sindicales declararon que su prioridad es acabar con lo que describen como trato discriminatorio, en lugar de las elevadas primas por firma de contrato que suelen figurar en las negociaciones salariales de la minería chilena. Antofagasta rechaza las acusaciones de que las diferencias salariales y de beneficios constituyan discriminación, argumentando que se deben a convenios colectivos distintos negociados en momentos diferentes. La empresa afirmó que sigue dispuesta a continuar las conversaciones y ha ofrecido un aumento real del 2% en los salarios base y una bonificación en efectivo de casi US$23.000 para cada uno. La empresa ha mantenido sus previsiones de producción a pesar de la huelga de 709 trabajadores, que representan aproximadamente el 22% de la plantilla de Centinela. Los sindicatos afirman que el impacto de la huelga se irá acumulando con el tiempo, y prevén que la producción de cobre podría caer alrededor de un 50% en noviembre si la huelga continúa. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

items.title: Queen Camilla on the joy of reading despite king's laughter and her tears
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Britain's Queen Camilla and King Charles spend their evenings reading before dinner, a quiet time which is interrupted by either his laughter or her tears, she told a documentary aimed at reversing the decline in reading for enjoyment in the UK.
items.body:
Britain's Queen Camilla and King Charles spend their evenings reading before dinner, a quiet time which is interrupted by either his laughter or her tears, she told a documentary aimed at reversing the decline in reading for enjoyment in the UK.
"When I'm deep in a book, I'll hear him roaring with laughter about something. It's very off-putting," she said, giving a rare glimpse of their private life at Clarence House.
"Or I'll suddenly start weeping."
Camilla, 79, has been a keen reader her whole life. After the success of a pandemic-era book club she set up on social media, she launched a charity to promote the benefits of reading three years ago.
In Britain, the percentage of children and young people who enjoy books hit its lowest level in 20 years last year, according to the National Literacy Trust, which is now working with the government and Camilla's charity to try to turn this around.
"I left school quite young, so reading has been most of my education. You learn so much about people, about life," Camilla told the documentary, "The Book That Changed My Life", which will air on the BBC on Wednesday.
When Charles laughs out loud, Camilla knows he will be reading a book by "Jeeves and Wooster" creator P.G. Wodehouse. She said he also loved biographies, while she likes historical fiction and thrillers.
She said books helped her father survive more than two years as a prisoner of war in Germany in the early 1940s, an experience he then wrote a book about.
"You're not thinking of yourself when you're reading, you can immerse yourself into other people's lives and that does relieve the stress," she said.
Charles is still receiving treatment for [USN:L8N44G0CW TEXT:"cancer"] and managing the fallout from [USN:L8N3Z81KN TEXT:"the arrest"] of his brother, Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, who denies wrongdoing, as well as negotiating the relationship with his younger son, [USN:L8N4590QP TEXT:"Prince Harry"], who has returned from the US to live in Britain.
Meanwhile, "Swan Song: Diana, My Sister", a memoir by Charles Spencer, the brother of Charles' first wife, has become a bestseller. Buckingham Palace rejected in [USN:L8N4581JE TEXT:"unusually strong terms"] the book's version of conversations surrounding Diana's death in 1997.

items.body:
French policing under scrutiny as student protest injuries mount
Reuters | Updated: 10-10-2026 11:30 IST | Created: 10-10-2026 11:30 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

By Juliette Jabkhiro and Layli Foroudi PARIS/ARGENTEUIL, France, Oct 10 (Reuters) - F ourteen-year-old Eden suffered a broken jaw and multiple smashed teeth when he was struck by a tear gas canister directed towards him at close range by a police officer last week during student protests in France, his parents and family lawyer said.
The teenager had been sitting on a wall looking at his phone metres away from the protest in Saint-Ouen-l'Aumone, the lawyer said. An officer approached him and struck him with a baton, prompting Eden to respond with a kick, according to the local prosecutor. A second officer then fired a tear gas grenade with a Cougar launcher, hitting him in the face. "(The officer) shot him in the mouth and left him lying on the ground, without even calling the emergency services," said lawyer Elsa Marcel. The family, who asked for Eden's second name to be withheld to protect their privacy, has filed a complaint for attempted murder, she said.
A police spokesperson said they do not comment on ongoing investigations. According to the prosecutor’s office, the police officer said that he was seeking to protect himself and his colleagues after the student confronted police. The officer was placed under formal investigation on charges of assault by a public official resulting in permanent disability or disfigurement on Tuesday, eight days after the incident. The case is one of 24 under investigation by the IGPN internal police watchdog linked to the policing of a more-than-two-week-long wave of student unrest over conditions in schools. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu has described the demonstrations as the most violent in decades.
The police response has renewed calls for the withdrawal of the use of rubber bullets and grenade launchers, which are not used by police in many other European countries and have been repeatedly criticised in recent years by rights groups, including Amnesty International and UN human rights experts, as dangerous and disproportionate. It has also sparked anger among the public and fanned support for a protest movement that is the latest manifestation of deep-seated discontent with President Emmanuel Macron’s government ahead of a 2027 election.
Via interviews and reviews of legal documents, Reuters has documented 28 cases of injuries suffered due to police force, of which 15 are among those under investigation by the IGPN. They involve the use of rubber bullets, stun grenades, tear gas, batons and charges on horseback. In two cases, a person's eye has been lost or injured due to rubber bullets. In another, a 15-year-old in Lens had his hand blown off — likely by a stun grenade, according to interior minister Laurent Nunez, who paused the use of stun grenades pending an investigation into the case.
Nunez said on Wednesday in a radio interview that about 200 students had been injured, but that it was very rarely the result of police action. “Our primary role is, of course, to protect high school students,” he said. Authorities said that 700 police officers have also been injured, schools have been burned or ransacked, and teachers and members of the public have been attacked. The police have arrested 6,877 people, mostly minors.
“France is an anomaly in terms of its use of arms and the number of victims — we have four irreversible injuries in the space of 12 days, and they are minors,” said Sebastian Roche, researcher on policing at the French National Centre for Scientific Research. “It is a level that is unknown in (France’s) contemporary history,” he said.
CALLS TO BAN 'LESS LETHAL' WEAPONS Roche said that France stands out in Europe for its use of "less lethal" weapons such as rubber bullets and stun grenades. Such weapons are generally not used for public order policing in Britain, Italy and Germany, aside from Hamburg, and although permitted in Spain, have caused fewer injuries than in France, said Roche.
In the Paris suburb of Argenteuil, a 16-year-old student on his way home after finding his school closed was shot by police, injuring his left eye, which may be permanently damaged, his lawyer Sophia Kerbaa told Reuters. It is not clear if he was hit by a rubber bullet or something else, she added. A video viewed by Reuters showed the boy bleeding from his eye.
“He was in the wrong place at the wrong time ... he is injured and in shock,” Kerbaa said. The prosecutor investigating the case said that, according to the police account, the injured student “seemed to correspond” to one of two young people who had directed fireworks at police officers, who responded with rubber bullets.
The interior ministry did not respond to questions on the case, or that of Eden. Human rights advocates, including Amnesty International, and some politicians have called for “less lethal” weapons to be banned permanently, while police unions say the police need these weapons to enforce order in violent situations and to ensure their own security.
“We must withdraw the use of rubber bullets and ... aim for zero injured students. That will allow us to de-escalate,” Mayor Bally Bagayoko of the left-wing France Unbowed party told Reuters. Bagayoko joined the protests in his town Saint-Denis, saying he wanted to protect young people from the police. Thierry Clair, a police union representative, said that serious injuries such as Eden’s, or another child losing his hand, were tragedies, but should not call into question France’s policing techniques. He said the problem came instead from the intensity of the violence being committed by some young people who stoked tensions.
“How do we respond when people are moving towards confrontation? If we remove intermediate force options, all we are left with is lethal force,” Clair told Reuters. “That is simply inconceivable.”

items.body:
Cricket-New Zealand's O'Rourke ruled out of India series
Reuters | Updated: 10-10-2026 11:23 IST | Created: 10-10-2026 11:23 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

New Zealand fast-bowler Will O'Rourke will miss the series against India as he continues his rehabilitation from injuries to his left hamstring and calf, the country's cricket board said on Saturday. O'Rourke suffered a hamstring tear during New Zealand's test series win over England in June, before hurting his calf in training in late August.
The 25-year-old will aim to return to full fitness ahead of a four-test tour of neighbours Australia beginning on December 9. "It's obviously disappointing for Will to have to miss such a marquee tour at home against India," New Zealand coach Rob Walter said in a statement.
"He was set to feature in both the ODI and test series, but following subsequent discussions, we all agreed it was best for him to take some more time to rehabilitate both injuries and safely build up his bowling loads. "Our pace bowling resources will be critical over the next few months so we're taking a conservative approach to Will's return to ensure he's fully fit before he takes the field again."
New Zealand host India in five Twenty20 internationals, five one-day internationals and two tests, with the opening T20 in Christchurch on October 22.

items.title: Colombia firma nueve contratos mineros con inversiones proyectadas de 16,8 millones de dólares
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Colombia firmó nueve contratos especiales de exploración y explotación de minerales estratégicos, como cobre, oro y fosfatos, con los que proyecta inversiones cercanas a 54.000 millones de pesos (16,8 millones de dólares), informó el viernes la Agencia Nacional de Minería (ANM).
items.body:
Colombia firmó nueve contratos especiales de exploración y explotación de minerales estratégicos, como cobre, oro y fosfatos, con los que proyecta inversiones cercanas a 54.000 millones de pesos (16,8 millones de dólares), informó el viernes la Agencia Nacional de Minería (ANM).
Los contratos se firmaron dentro de las Rondas Mineras 2026 y corresponden a Áreas Estratégicas Mineras en los departamentos de Cesar, La Guajira, Antioquia, Tolima y Huila, precisó un comunicado de la entidad.
Ocho contratos son de la ronda de cobre, oro y polimetálicos, y uno es de la ronda de fosfatos.
Entre las empresas que recibieron los contratos se encuentran la china Zijin Mining y OP Gold Capital, informó la ANM.
Este modelo de contratación busca dar más seguridad jurídica a los inversionistas y reducir los riesgos, los conflictos y los tiempos de desarrollo de los proyectos, de acuerdo con la ANM.
"Sigamos haciendo estos esfuerzos de generar más minería, más desarrollo, más riqueza, mejor economía, mejor educación para todas las regiones de Colombia", dijo el presidente de la ANM, Juan Camilo Valencia, citado en el comunicado.
Al mismo tiempo, la agencia firmó 44 nuevas titulaciones mineras en 14 departamentos. Antioquia tiene el mayor número, con 10 títulos, seguida de Huila con nueve, Chocó con seis y Norte de Santander con cinco.
Entre esos títulos hay 19 contratos de concesión: 11 de mediana minería y ocho de pequeña minería, que cubren minerales metálicos, materiales de construcción, minerales industriales y carbón.
(1 dólar = 3.218,75 pesos)

items.title: Sequoia-backed chip startup Nuvacore raising funds at about a $2.5 billion valuation, sources say
items.author: Max Cherney, Krystal Hu
items.creator: Max Cherney, Krystal Hu
items.summary: Six-month-old microchip startup Nuvacore, which does not yet have a product, is raising hundreds of millions of dollars at a roughly $2.5 billion valuation to develop a new central processor designed for data centers, according to two people familiar with the fundraising.
items.body:
Six-month-old microchip startup Nuvacore, which does not yet have a product, is raising hundreds of millions of dollars at a roughly $2.5 billion valuation to develop a new central processor designed for data centers, according to two people familiar with the fundraising.
Nuvacore is seeking to raise the funds as the appetite for central processors has swollen due to the thirst for data-crunching capacity to power chatbots such as Anthropic's Claude. CPUs perform vital functions as traffic controllers for Nvidia's AI chips and run autonomous AI software known as agents.
The roughly $2.5 billion valuation has not been previously reported. The Information reported previously that Nuvacore was raising $200 million or more. The funding round has not closed, and the people cautioned that the valuation and size of the capital raise could change.
Intel (INTC.O) and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD.O) , which use x86 technology, have long dominated the data center CPU market. Companies designing chips based on Arm's technology — found inside Amazon and Microsoft custom CPUs — have also attempted to make inroads in the data center market.
Nuvacore has not yet developed a product. Last month, it described an unconventional design strategy: to build the core functionality of the chip before committing to an architecture such as the x86 used by Intel and AMD, or Arm, which is used in most mobile phones.
The design strategy will allow the company's engineers to avoid the limitations and requirements of specific architectures and optimize a design for the type of computations that are most common in data centers and AI infrastructure, Nuvacore said.
Nuvacore declined to comment.
The San Jose, California-based startup was founded by renowned engineers Gerard Williams, John Bruno and Ram Srinivasan. Williams, a former Apple (AAPL.O) executive, sold a prior startup called Nuvia to Qualcomm (QCOM.O) for [USN:KBN29I1OO TEXT:"$1.4 billion in 2021"].
Nuvacore earlier this year announced a seed funding round led by Sequoia Capital. It joins a series of young chip startups that have sought billion-dollar valuations before releasing a product as investor appetite for AI hardware companies has returned.
Over the past decade, Silicon Valley venture capital firms have taken much less interest in hardware than software because of hardware's longer development cycles, higher capital needs and the industry's cyclical demand.
Investors put about $10.7 billion into semiconductor startups in the first five months of 2026, already outpacing the $12.2 billion raised globally in all of 2025, according to Crunchbase data.
Earlier this year, Intel said it could not manufacture enough chips to meet demand, and was able to sell products it had previously determined were too faulty for sale. AMD also described swelling CPU sales in a recent results conference call with analysts.
Shares in both companies have risen more than 180% this year.
Nvidia (NVDA.O) launched a CPU called Vera this year. CEO Jensen Huang has said the company expects to [USN:L4N41V0P1 TEXT:"sell $20 billion worth"] of its Vera CPU in this fiscal year, which ends in January.

Intel and Advanced Micro Devices, which use x86 technology, have long dominated the data center CPU market. Companies designing chips based on Arm's technology — found inside Amazon and Microsoft custom CPUs — have also attempted to make inroads in the data center market.

Nuvacore has not yet developed a product. Last month, it described an unconventional design strategy: to build the core functionality of the chip before committing to an architecture such as the x86 used by Intel and AMD, or Arm, which is used in most mobile phones. 
The design strategy will allow the company's engineers to avoid the limitations and requirements of specific architectures and optimize a design for the type of computations that are most common in data centers and AI infrastructure, Nuvacore said.
Nuvacore declined to comment.
The San Jose, California-based startup was founded by renowned engineers Gerard Williams, John Bruno and Ram Srinivasan. Williams, a former Apple executive, sold a prior startup called Nuvia to Qualcomm for $1.4 billion in 2021.
Nuvacore earlier this year announced a seed funding round led by Sequoia Capital. It joins a series of young chip startups that have sought billion-dollar valuations before releasing a product as investor appetite for AI hardware companies has returned.
Over the past decade, Silicon Valley venture capital firms have taken much less interest in hardware than software because of hardware's longer development cycles, higher capital needs and the industry's cyclical demand.
Investors put about $10.7 billion into semiconductor startups in the first five months of 2026, already outpacing the $12.2 billion raised globally in all of 2025, according to Crunchbase data.
Earlier this year, Intel said it could not manufacture enough chips to meet demand, and was able to sell products it had previously determined were too faulty for sale. AMD also described swelling CPU sales in a recent results conference call with analysts.
Shares in both companies have risen more than 180 per cent this year.
Nvidia launched a CPU called Vera this year. CEO Jensen Huang has said the company expects to sell $20 billion worth of its Vera CPU in this fiscal year, which ends in January.

items.title: Super Micro contractor pleads guilty in scheme to divert AI servers with Nvidia chips to China
items.author: Karen Freifeld, Jaspreet Singh
items.creator: Karen Freifeld, Jaspreet Singh
items.summary: A contractor linked to Super Micro Computer has pleaded guilty in a scheme to illegally export computer servers containing advanced Nvidia AI chips to China, a federal court filing showed on Friday.
items.body:
A contractor linked to Super Micro Computer (SMCI.O) has pleaded guilty in a scheme to illegally export computer servers containing advanced Nvidia (NVDA.O) AI chips to China, a federal court filing showed on Friday.
Ting-Wei "Willy" Sun pleaded guilty to four counts, including conspiracies to violate US export controls, smuggle goods from the US, defraud the country and obstruct justice. He entered the plea on Thursday in U.S. District Court in Manhattan.
The United States and China are competing for dominance in AI, with both investing billions of dollars in a technology seen as critical to economic growth, national security and military capabilities.
In March, [USN:L1N4071M5 TEXT:"prosecutors charged"] Sun and two others associated with Super Micro, including a co-founder of the AI-server maker, with conspiring to divert about $2.5 billion worth of US AI technology to China in violation of export laws.
The scheme began around October 2023, with Sun and others conspiring to export servers from a US manufacturer, widely believed to be Super Micro, to China without the required licenses, according to the indictment.
Asked for comment on the guilty plea, California-based Super Micro referred to its prior statements that the company was not named as a defendant in the indictment and that it had no impact on its business operations. [USN:L4N40Q1GS TEXT:"Super Micro"] terminated Sun and cut ties with the other defendants earlier this year.
A lawyer for Sun declined to comment.
Also indicted were the co-founder Yih-Shyan "Wally" Liaw and Ruei-Tsang "Steven" Chang, who was a sales manager at Super Micro's Taiwan office, while Sun was a contractor.
A lawyer for Liaw - who co-founded Super Micro in 1993 and joined its board in 2023 - did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Chang's lawyer could not immediately be reached for comment.
The indictment described Sun as a broker and “fixer” who facilitated orders and took steps to conceal the scheme. He helped stage "dummy" servers in December 2025 and made false statements to a US Department of Commerce officer during an inspection of supposedly stored servers, which had already been diverted to China, according to the indictment.
Washington has restricted sales of advanced AI chips to China, citing national security concerns. The indictment said Nvidia's B200, H100 and H200 graphics processing units, and servers containing them, were subject to the restrictions.

items.title: ATUALIZA 1 CSN negocia com grupo espanhol venda da SWT por 550 mi de euros
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: A CSN anunciou nesta sexta-feira assinatura de acordo vinculante para venda de sua usina de aços longos na Alemanha, atribuindo um valor para o negócio de 550 milhões de euros, segundo fato relevante.
items.body:
A CSN (CSNA3.SA) anunciou nesta sexta-feira assinatura de acordo vinculante para venda de sua usina de aços longos na Alemanha, atribuindo um valor para o negócio de 550 milhões de euros, segundo fato relevante.
A companhia, que está tentando reduzir endividamento, afirmou que o termo vinculante foi assinado pela espanhola Bipadosa, controladora do grupo siderúrgico espanhol Megasa.
O período de exclusividade para assinatura de documentos definitivos para a conclusão do negócio é de 10 semanas, afirmou a CSN.
A SWT foi comprada pela CSN em 2012. Na época o valor anunciado pela companhia brasileira para o negócio foi de 482,5 milhões de euros. "considerando a premissa de endividamento zero".
A usina alemã tem capacidade instalada de 1,1 milhão de toneladas de aços longos por ano.
"A potencial alienação das ações da SWT representa mais um passo importante no programa de desinvestimentos da CSN com o propósito de reduzir o seu atual nível de endividamento", afirmou a CSN no fato relevante.
Nos resultados de segundo trimestre deste ano, a CSN afirmou que a SWT havia atingido sua melhor marca de vendas desde o primeiro trimestre de 2022, com 205 mil toneladas.
Além da Alemanha, a CSN tem presença em Portugal por meio da produtora de aços planos Lusosider.
A empresa ainda não havia citado publicamente a SWT como alvo de venda, embora executivos da companhia tenham citado nos últimos trimestres que a CSN estava aberta a avaliar alternativas e parcerias para suas operações siderúrgicas.
Em outros mercados internacionais, a CSN chegou a ter usinas nos Estados Unidos, mas vendeu esses ativos para norte-americana Steel Dynamics (STLD.O) em 2018.
No Brasil, a CSN anunciou em agosto que recebeu propostas vinculantes por sua produtora de [USN:L6N4470LD TEXT:"cimento"]. Na época, as fontes afirmaram à Reuters que as principais concorrentes pela CSN Cimentos eram a chinesa Huaxin (600801.SS) e um consórcio formado por Votorantim e Cementir (CEMI.MI) , de origem italiana, e que as propostas deveriam ultrapassar os R$10 bilhões.
A CSN terminou junho com alavancagem financeira de 3,49 vezes e dívida líquida de R$42,1 bilhões.

items.title: Boarded windows and evacuations as major hurricane nears US Gulf coast
items.author: Andrew Hay
items.creator: Andrew Hay
items.summary: Residents of coastal towns in Florida and Alabama boarded windows and filled sandbags on Friday as Hurricane Isaias bore down on the US Gulf Coast, bringing with it life-threatening storm surge and 115 mph (185 kph) winds.
items.body:
Residents of coastal towns in Florida and Alabama boarded windows and filled sandbags on Friday as Hurricane Isaias bore down on the US Gulf Coast, bringing with it life-threatening storm surge and 115 mph (185 kph) winds.
Tens of thousands of people in Florida's Panhandle and Alabama's Gulf Coast faced mandatory evacuation orders. Local television stations showed roads packed with vehicles heading north, away from the water.
The Category 3 Isaias, the first hurricane of an unusually quiet season for the United States, was expected to make landfall between Mobile, Alabama, and Grayton Beach in the Florida Panhandle on Friday evening, according to the National Hurricane Center.
The 90-mile (145 km) stretch of coast is known for brilliant-white sand beaches, with some areas packed with vacation homes next to small coastal towns like Destin, Florida.
"If you've been asked to evacuate, get out now, conditions are only going to deteriorate," NHC Director Michael Brennan told Fox Weather on Friday. "That surge is going to come in after dark, that's not a place you are going to want to be in."
Scientists say human-caused climate change has warmed the Gulf of Mexico, possibly intensifying hurricanes like Isaias.
The storm will pack sustained winds capable of extensive structural damage to beach houses, though modern homes built to strict coastal codes may remain standing. Storm surge of up to 9 feet (2.7 meters) was forecast around the Alabama-Florida border.
President Donald Trump [USN:L1N45V0XC TEXT:"canceled"] a planned trip to Alabama on Saturday for the Georgia vs. Alabama college football game, as the hurricane is expected to affect Tuscaloosa, the city where the contest was set to be played.
Up to 15 inches (38 cm) of rain was expected in localized areas of the Florida Panhandle and the Big Bend area.
Oil companies have evacuated personnel from 129 [USN:L1N45V0PT TEXT:"oil and gas"] production platforms, representing 35% of the 371 staffed platforms in the Gulf of Mexico.
Hurricane-force winds were expected as far as 100 miles inland in southern Alabama, possibly triggering tornadoes. Some 2 to 5 inches (5 to 13 cm) of rain were expected across the US Southeast as far north as the southern Appalachian Mountains and coastal areas of the Carolinas.

items.title: Taxed pitching staffs will decide Game 5 between Guardians, White Sox
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: CLEVELAND -- The American League Division Series has provided a roller coaster of emotions for the Cleveland Guardians and Chicago White Sox.
items.body:
CLEVELAND -- The American League Division Series has provided a roller coaster of emotions for the Cleveland Guardians and Chicago White Sox.
Road teams have won the first four contests, setting up a winner-take-all Game 5 on Saturday night.
Guardians right-hander Gavin Williams (0-0, 3.00 ERA) takes on White Sox right-hander Sean Burke (1-0, 3.86 ERA) in a battle of traditional starters.
The Tampa Bay Rays await the victor in the AL Championship Series.
"Obviously, it's an honor to be able to start this game and go out there and do my thing for the guys," said Burke, who allowed one run in 5 1/3 innings as the bulk reliever in Game 2.
"I empty the tank every single time I'm out there, so this is no different. I'm giving 100% of everything I have."
Williams had been penciled in three days earlier, but his availability became a question mark after he came out of the bullpen for the final three outs Thursday in Cleveland's 9-5 win in Game 4.
According to Guardians manager Stephen Vogt, "The Big Rig" earned the right to make the decision himself. The staff ace did so shortly after walking off the field.
"The body feels good right now, been in the training room all morning just figuring it out," said Williams, who threw 18 pitches in his first career relief outing.
"I throw a (bullpen session) on those (specific off) days, and everybody knows it. Just being able to feel the mound in a game-like situation is even better at that point."
It's essentially a rematch of Game 2, when Williams struck out 11 over five-plus innings and allowed two runs. Burke was the winning pitcher as Chicago rallied for a 4-3 triumph Monday.
Burke has been brilliant against the Guardians this season, going 3-0 with a 1.19 ERA over 22 2/3 innings. He has won in Cleveland in his last two matchups, giving up one earned run in 10 1/3 frames.
"I've really seen his confidence grow," White Sox manager Will Venable said. "It's how he finishes his pitches, how he walks around the mound after he gets an out. Sean is a guy that's got the right mentality to figure out a way to get it done."
Williams' work against the White Sox has been a mixed bag, with an 0-1 record and a 3.76 ERA in six total appearances (five starts). He has struck out 40 over 26 1/3 innings and averaged 5.1 innings per start.
"Gavin wants the ball, we want him to have the ball, and it's his game," Vogt said. "The game will tell us when it's time to move on, or maybe he takes it the whole way. We don't know. We've got to get there and find out."
Of more concern for Cleveland is closer Cade Smith, who pitched two innings in Game 3 and was going to do the same in Game 4 until faltering in the ninth. The MLB saves co-leader tossed 50 total pitches.
White Sox counterpart Grant Taylor, who earned saves in the first two games, declared himself good to go after a disastrous four-run, zero-out night in Game 4.
Smith, however, spent Friday receiving treatment at the ballpark and opted out of a scheduled press conference.
"I don't know if it's something that we can push to a ton of pitches with Cade," Vogt admitted. "But when you have to play three straight elimination games, there's going to be some high volume."
The series began with a pair of games in Cleveland, where White Sox pitchers held the hosts to seven total hits. Munetaka Murakami and Braden Montgomery provided the go-ahead RBIs.
Chicago's dreams of clinching in the Windy City were dashed by Jose Ramirez and Jo Adell, who each totaled five RBIs as the Central Division-champion Guardians scored nine runs in both Games 3 and 4.
As a result, the division rivals will contest the 40th ALDS Game 5 under the current format. Home teams are 18-21 all-time.
"We're obviously thinking about the game and the situation a lot," Cleveland second baseman Travis Bazzana said. "You'll get some butterflies, some nerves, and a little bit of a good heart rate as we get closer and closer to game time."
--Brian Dulik, Field Level Media

items.title: Broncos OC Davis Webb disappointed to lose play-calling role
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Denver Broncos offensive coordinator Davis Webb didn't envision getting only four games to show off his abilities as a play-caller.
items.body:
Denver Broncos offensive coordinator Davis Webb didn't envision getting only four games to show off his abilities as a play-caller.
Webb said Friday "it's not ideal" to be stripped of the duties so early in the season. Head coach Sean Payton has taken over and will call the plays for Sunday's road game against the Los Angeles Chargers.
By all accounts, that is a small sample size for a change to be made when it comes to a new play-caller.
"Luckily that's not my job, that's (Payton's) job," Webb said Friday. "I think he answered that. I think the world of him, how we've gone about it ... it's not ideal, but in the same breath, we're 2-2 in the first four games, our first four opponents were a combined 13-3 to start the season. Welcome to the league."
The Broncos rank 27th in scoring offense (18.5 points per game) and 28th in total offense (280.3 yards per game) while scoring 20 or fewer points in three of their first four games.
Criticisms about Webb began immediately when Denver was routed 31-10 in its season opener on Monday Night Football by the Kansas City Chiefs.
Others question Webb being in the role since he is just 31 years old and only in his fourth season of coaching.
Webb felt he was ready for the play-calling role when he was promoted to offensive coordinator in the offseason.
"I taught myself early to think about the best- and worst-case scenarios," Webb said. "And if you're OK with both, then take that job on. It is what it is, nothing I can do about it now except be the best offensive coordinator I can be and that's what I'm trying to do."
Broncos quarterback Bo Nix has passed for 819 yards, five touchdowns and three interceptions this season. He is completing 60% of his passes after hitting on 63.4% last season and 66.3% as a rookie in 2024.
Webb threw 40 NFL passes - all in his lone start in 2022 for the New York Giants. He spent six NFL seasons between active rosters and practice squads with the Giants (2017, 2022), New York Jets (2018) and Buffalo Bills (2019-21). He was a third-round pick in the 2017 NFL Draft.
Webb played three seasons at Texas Tech (2013-15) and had a monster 2016 season at Cal with 4,295 yards and 37 touchdowns against 12 interceptions.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Kremlin says Putin in phone call with Trump downplays immediate Ukraine talks resumption
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin told US President Donald Trump on Friday that Kyiv had undermined the possibility of an immediate resumption of trilateral Ukraine peace talks after it had hit Moscow with drones during last month's election, the Kremlin said.
items.body:
Russian President Vladimir Putin told US President Donald Trump on Friday that Kyiv had undermined the possibility of an immediate resumption of trilateral Ukraine peace talks after it had hit Moscow with drones during last month's election, the Kremlin said.
Trump has so far unsuccessfully tried to broker a peace deal to end the war in Ukraine , which started with Russia's invasion in February 2022.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Thursday that Russia's war in Ukraine is at a [USN:L1N45U0GU TEXT:"dangerous stalemate"] and the United States will keep working toward a settlement to end the conflict.
Putin had said that Moscow had been [USN:L1N45H0MX TEXT:"ready to resume"] negotiations with Kyiv after last month's Russian parliamentary elections, but Ukraine launched attacks on Moscow and hit polling stations, putting the peace process in jeopardy, according to him.
"By launching a massive drone attack on Moscow, other cities and polling stations, as well as on specific individuals involved in organising the election, on the main voting day, the Kyiv regime effectively disrupted the possibility of an immediate resumption of the negotiation process," Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov said about the call with Trump.
"And now, as the president said, we will consider when those negotiations can be resumed," he added, referring to trilateral negotiations involving the US, Russia and Ukraine.
Ushakov also said Putin and Trump discussed major economic initiatives during the phone call, including potential supplies of Russian fuel.
Trump said earlier on Friday after the call with Putin that Russia had agreed to immediately [USN:L1N45V0MW TEXT:"supply diesel"] to US and global markets in an effort to lower fuel prices ahead of the US midterm elections next month, although analysts said the amounts would likely not reduce prices greatly.

items.title: Sem orientação clara da campanha, base pró-Lula se mobiliza nas ruas e nas redes
items.author: Lisandra Paraguassu
items.creator: Lisandra Paraguassu
items.summary: Cinco dias depois de terminado o primeiro turno, o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula fez nesta sexta-feira sua primeira agenda externa, mas enquanto seu partido tenta se reorganizar depois da derrota inicial para Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), grupos regionais, estudantes, influenciadores e organizações de fãs, os chamados fandoms, foram para as ruas, mesmo sem orientações claras.
items.body:
Cinco dias depois de terminado o primeiro turno, o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula fez nesta sexta-feira sua primeira agenda externa, mas enquanto seu partido tenta se reorganizar depois da derrota inicial para Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), grupos regionais, estudantes, influenciadores e organizações de fãs, os chamados fandoms, foram para as ruas, mesmo sem orientações claras.
Já desde terça-feira, passada a derrota por quase 2 pontos percentuais, grupos começaram a se organizar pela internet. Na quarta-feira, milhares de estudantes foram às ruas no Rio de Janeiro contra a eleição de Flávio Bolsonaro. Desde então, houve manifestações de estudantes em pelo menos 10 Estados.
No domingo, na Paulista, outra marcha está sendo organizada pela União Nacional dos Estudantes (UNE), apoiada por fã-clubes de centenas de artistas pop, que foram às redes declarar apoio ao presidente e se oferecer para ocupar as redes em defesa da campanha do presidente.
"Vocês viram as manifestações dos estudantes. São iniciativas próprias, voluntárias, de quem não quer o risco desse país voltar ao modelo que teve no governo Bolsonaro", disse o senador Camilo Santana, que se incorporou à coordenação da campanha neste segundo turno.
O que parece ser um ponto positivo, no entanto, acaba por dar razão a queixas de aliados: quase uma semana se passou das três de campanha nesse segundo turno e pouca ou quase nenhuma orientação veio da coordenação da campanha, que tenta se reestruturar com novos nomes depois de enormes críticas de aliados à condução da campanha no primeiro turno.
"Não recebemos nada, mas não vamos parar. A gente está fazendo o que pode, tem mobilização todo dia", diz uma fonte de campanha regional.
Só não tem o presidente.
Lula fez nesta sexta-feira uma caminhada em Ceilândia, cidade-satélite de Brasília, seu primeiro evento de campanha. No sábado, tem outro evento no Rio Grande do Norte, mas a agenda para por aí. No domingo, quem deve ir à Paulista com os estudantes é o vice-presidente Geraldo Alckmin.
Camilo Santana afirma que o presidente irá a Minas, São Paulo e vários Estados, mas a agenda ainda não está definida.
"Não tem como ir a todos os Estados", disse.
Um parlamentar que participou das reuniões esta semana disse à Reuters que, mesmo sem orientações específicas, os parlamentares e candidatos, mesmo os que não foram eleitos, estão mantendo suas estruturas para tentar ajudar na campanha nacional como podem.
Na quinta-feira, em São Paulo, o ministro da Secretaria-Geral da Presidência, Guilherme Boulos, o ex-ministro Fernando Haddad, candidato derrotado ao governo de São Paulo e diversos deputados eleitos fizeram uma "plenária de mobilização, na zona central de São Paulo, para organizar mutirões de panfletagem.
No mesmo dia, à tarde, Haddad foi à Paulista distribuir panfletos.
É nas redes que a interação subiu, com diversos grupos e influenciadores não apenas declarando voto, mas usando o alcance para marcar manifestações e falar não apenas de propostas, mas do que veem como riscos de um futuro governo Flávio Bolsonaro e dividindo estratégias para mudar votos.
items.raw_description: Cinco dias depois de terminado o primeiro turno, o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula fez nesta sexta-feira sua primeira agenda externa, mas enquanto seu partido tenta se reorganizar depois da derrota inicial para Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), grupos regionais, estudantes, influenciadores e organizações de fãs, os chamados fandoms, foram para as ruas, mesmo sem orientações claras.

items.title: Kalshi probes suspicious trades tied to Trump press secretary pick, WSJ reports
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Prediction market Kalshi has launched an investigation into suspicious trades tied to the selection of Katie Zacharia as U.S. President Donald Trump's new White House press secretary, the Wall Street Journal reported on Friday, citing a company spokesperson.
items.body:
Prediction market Kalshi has launched an investigation into suspicious trades tied to the selection of Katie Zacharia as U.S. President Donald Trump's new White House press secretary, the Wall Street Journal reported on Friday, citing a company spokesperson.
Kalshi declined to comment on the report.
Here are some details:
At least three small wagers were placed before news of Zacharia's selection emerged, potentially netting traders thousands of dollars in profits, the Journal reported.
A $19 bet placed late on Thursday is set to pay $1,896, while wagers of about $74 and $80 placed on Friday are expected to pay $3,689 and $4,023, respectively.
Zacharia, a conservative commentator who previously worked briefly at the Department of Homeland Security, had been given about a 1% chance of securing the role on Kalshi before the announcement.
Prediction markets, where users wager on outcomes ranging from sporting contests to world events, have faced growing scrutiny over the risk of traders profiting from inside information.
In July, Trump's teleprompter operator came under investigation by the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission over potential insider trading.

items.summary: Read more about NEWSMAKER-Pressure mounts on India poll chief Gyanesh Kumar over voter list changes on Devdiscourse ...
items.body:
NEWSMAKER-Pressure mounts on India poll chief Gyanesh Kumar over voter list changes
Reuters | Updated: 10-10-2026 10:33 IST | Created: 10-10-2026 10:33 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

India's "Cockroach" youth movement and opposition parties are pushing hard for election chief Gyanesh Kumar to resign over accusations of widespread manipulation of voter lists during an exercise to verify one billion voters. The calls come a month after US President Donald Trump praised the former bureaucrat, who took over as India's chief election commissioner in February 2025, for insisting that voters prove their identity with photo ID, unlike in the US.
Criticism of Kumar, who has denied all accusations, soared last month after a report in the Indian Express newspaper. The paper said his two deputies had raised at least 14 formal objections over 10 months to decisions regarding voter rolls, registration procedures and the poll body's digital systems.
Election Commission data shows that more than 130 million names, a figure exceeding the population of Japan, have been struck off the voter list since the latest round of revisions began last year. Nearly 650 million people of the 960 million registered voted in the last general election in 2024.
The opposition has long claimed that the government is trying to fix voter lists to its advantage and was quick to repeat the accusations after the Indian Express report. Government ministers, Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party and the poll body have all denied the charges.
Kumar, 62, and the two other election commissioners have not commented, but the Election Commission said, "Differing views and observations are a normal part of deliberation in any institution". PROTEST THREAT
The youth-led Cockroach Janta Party has called a protest in New Delhi on Saturday to demand Kumar's resignation, and the main opposition alliance led by the Congress party has also staged protests this week calling for him to step down. Kumar has defended the actions of the poll body and told a press conference last year: "For the Election Commission, there is neither an opposition nor a ruling side; everyone is equal."
When Trump praised him, Kumar was riding high in sections of the Indian media last month. But since the Indian Express report, graffiti have appeared near his ancestral home in northern India calling him a traitor. Kumar joined the Indian Administrative Service in 1988 after completing his B.Tech in civil engineering from an elite government college in his northern home state of Uttar Pradesh.
He previously worked in the defence and home ministries, and retired in January 2024. Two months later he was appointed an election commissioner, before eventually becoming the chief.
Kumar has had a troubled relationship with opposition parties from the start of his tenure as chief. Opposition lawmakers presented a motion in parliament for his removal this year, but it was rejected.

items.title: Two Sidus Space directors resign, citing governance disagreements
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Satellite technology firm Sidus Space said on Friday two directors had resigned from its board, citing disagreements over governance and management practices.
items.body:
Satellite technology firm Sidus Space (SIDU.O) said on Friday two directors had resigned from its board, citing disagreements over governance and management practices.
The company said it disagreed with the assertions made by the directors in their resignation letters. Here are some details:
Tiffany Norwood and Kelle Wendling resigned from Sidus Space's board effective October 6, according to a regulatory filing.
Norwood, chair of the audit committee and a member of the corporate governance and nominating committee, cited "a number of concerns and disagreements", including the handling of a confidential complaint brought to her and other committee chairs.
Wendling, a member of the audit, compensation, and corporate governance and nominating committees, said she resigned after considering matters related to the company's management and governance.
Sidus Space included both directors' resignation letters in the regulatory filing.
"I have previously raised concerns regarding these matters through the appropriate Board and committee processes, and those concerns remain unresolved," Wendling said in her letter.
The company said it had notified Norwood and Wendling of its disclosures and given them an opportunity to state whether they agreed with its response.
